`src/input/wayland_interpose.cc`:

```cc
// Wayland event interposition for input blocking.
//
// On Wayland, there is no XGrabPointer equivalent. The game and our overlay
// both receive pointer/keyboard events from the compositor for the same
// surface. This module interposes on wl_proxy_add_listener and
// wl_proxy_add_dispatcher (the underlying C functions that the generated
// protocol helpers use) and wraps the game's pointer/keyboard callbacks.
//
// Blocking is a hitbox, not a global gate: the overlay publishes its rects,
// and only events positioned inside them are withheld from the game. Pointer
// motion/button/axis carry or inherit a position; keyboard has none, so it
// follows the last pointer position.
//
// Overlay-owned proxies are registered via registerOverlayProxy() and are
// always passed through unwrapped.

#include "wayland_interpose.hh"
#include "input_blocker.hh"
#include "wayland_display.hh"
#include "wayland_syncobj_gate.hh"
#include "wayland_interpose_patch.hh"
#include "logger.hh"

// Forward-declare to avoid pulling in mouse_input_wayland.hh (which
// transitively includes mouse_input.hh → X11 headers in some targets).
namespace VkHook { void mirrorButtonState(uint32_t button, bool pressed); }

#include <wayland-client.h>
#include <dlfcn.h>
#include <atomic>
#include <cstring>
#include <mutex>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <unordered_set>
#include <string>
#include <algorithm>
#include <cstdlib>

namespace VkHook
{
    namespace
    {
        // Vulkan layers are typically loaded RTLD_LOCAL, which prevents global
        // symbol interposition in normal implicit-layer mode. Promote this
        // already-loaded object to RTLD_GLOBAL so our wl_proxy wrappers are
        // visible process-wide.
        __attribute__((constructor)) void promoteSelfToGlobalScope()
        {
            Dl_info info{};
            if (dladdr(reinterpret_cast<void*>(&promoteSelfToGlobalScope), &info) == 0 || !info.dli_fname)
                return;

            void* handle = dlopen(info.dli_fname, RTLD_NOLOAD | RTLD_NOW | RTLD_GLOBAL);
            if (!handle)
                handle = dlopen(info.dli_fname, RTLD_NOW | RTLD_GLOBAL);

            if (handle)
                Logger::debug("Wayland interpose: promoted VkHook library to RTLD_GLOBAL");
        }
    } // namespace

    static std::mutex proxyMutex;
    static std::unordered_set<wl_proxy*> overlayProxies;

    void registerOverlayProxy(wl_proxy* proxy)
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(proxyMutex);
        overlayProxies.insert(proxy);
    }

    void unregisterOverlayProxy(wl_proxy* proxy)
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(proxyMutex);
        overlayProxies.erase(proxy);
    }

    static bool isOverlayProxy(wl_proxy* proxy)
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(proxyMutex);
        return overlayProxies.count(proxy) > 0;
    }
} // namespace VkHook

// Last pointer position seen on a game pointer, in wl_surface-local coords.
// Events without coordinates (button, axis, key) are tested against this.
static std::atomic<double> g_lastPointerX{-1.0};
static std::atomic<double> g_lastPointerY{-1.0};

static bool pointerBlocked()
{
    return VkHook::isInputBlockedAt((float)g_lastPointerX.load(std::memory_order_acquire),
                                     (float)g_lastPointerY.load(std::memory_order_acquire));
}

// ── Game listener storage ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// Per-proxy data for wrapped game listeners. We store the game's original
// listener and user_data so we can forward events when not blocking.
struct GamePointerData
{
    wl_pointer_listener original;
    void* userData;
};

struct GameKeyboardData
{
    wl_keyboard_listener original;
    void* userData;
};

static std::mutex gameDataMutex;
static std::unordered_map<wl_pointer*, GamePointerData> gamePointers;
static std::unordered_map<wl_keyboard*, GameKeyboardData> gameKeyboards;

// Keys the game currently holds, tracked even while blocked so a hitbox
// crossing can release exactly those and re-press whatever is still held.
static std::unordered_map<wl_keyboard*, std::unordered_set<uint32_t>> gameHeldKeys;

struct GamePointerDispatcherData
{
    wl_dispatcher_func_t original;
    const void* dispatcherData;
};

struct GameKeyboardDispatcherData
{
    wl_dispatcher_func_t original;
    const void* dispatcherData;
};

static std::unordered_map<wl_proxy*, GamePointerDispatcherData> gamePointerDispatchers;
static std::unordered_map<wl_proxy*, GameKeyboardDispatcherData> gameKeyboardDispatchers;

// ── Wrapper pointer listener ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

static void wp_enter(void* data, wl_pointer* p, uint32_t serial, wl_surface* s, wl_fixed_t x, wl_fixed_t y)
{
    g_lastPointerX.store(wl_fixed_to_double(x), std::memory_order_release);
    g_lastPointerY.store(wl_fixed_to_double(y), std::memory_order_release);
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(gameDataMutex);
    auto it = gamePointers.find(p);
    if (it != gamePointers.end() && it->second.original.enter)
        it->second.original.enter(it->second.userData, p, serial, s, x, y);
}

static void wp_leave(void* data, wl_pointer* p, uint32_t serial, wl_surface* s)
{
    // Always forward leave — the game needs to know it lost focus
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(gameDataMutex);
    auto it = gamePointers.find(p);
    if (it != gamePointers.end() && it->second.original.leave)
        it->second.original.leave(it->second.userData, p, serial, s);
}

static void wp_motion(void* data, wl_pointer* p, uint32_t time, wl_fixed_t x, wl_fixed_t y)
{
    const double fx = wl_fixed_to_double(x);
    const double fy = wl_fixed_to_double(y);
    g_lastPointerX.store(fx, std::memory_order_release);
    g_lastPointerY.store(fy, std::memory_order_release);
    if (VkHook::isInputBlockedAt((float)fx, (float)fy))
        return;
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(gameDataMutex);
    auto it = gamePointers.find(p);
    if (it != gamePointers.end() && it->second.original.motion)
        it->second.original.motion(it->second.userData, p, time, x, y);
}

static void wp_button(void* data, wl_pointer* p, uint32_t serial, uint32_t time, uint32_t button, uint32_t state)
{
    // Always mirror button state to overlay — the game's pointer receives
    // releases via Wayland's implicit grab that our overlay pointer never sees.
    if (VkHook::isWayland())
        VkHook::mirrorButtonState(button, state == WL_POINTER_BUTTON_STATE_PRESSED);

    if (pointerBlocked())
        return;
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(gameDataMutex);
    auto it = gamePointers.find(p);
    if (it != gamePointers.end() && it->second.original.button)
        it->second.original.button(it->second.userData, p, serial, time, button, state);
}

static void wp_axis(void* data, wl_pointer* p, uint32_t time, uint32_t axis, wl_fixed_t value)
{
    if (pointerBlocked())
        return;
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(gameDataMutex);
    auto it = gamePointers.find(p);
    if (it != gamePointers.end() && it->second.original.axis)
        it->second.original.axis(it->second.userData, p, time, axis, value);
}

static void wp_frame(void* data, wl_pointer* p)
{
    if (pointerBlocked())
        return;
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(gameDataMutex);
    auto it = gamePointers.find(p);
    if (it != gamePointers.end() && it->second.original.frame)
        it->second.original.frame(it->second.userData, p);
}

static void wp_axis_source(void* data, wl_pointer* p, uint32_t source)

    .leave = wp_leave,

// ── Wrapper keyboard listener ────────────────────────────────────────────────

static void wk_keymap(void* data, wl_keyboard* kb, uint32_t format, int32_t fd, uint32_t size)
{
    // Always forward keymap — needed for initialization
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(gameDataMutex);
    auto it = gameKeyboards.find(kb);
    if (it != gameKeyboards.end() && it->second.original.keymap)
        it->second.original.keymap(it->second.userData, kb, format, fd, size);
}

static void wk_enter(void* data, wl_keyboard* kb, uint32_t serial, wl_surface* s, wl_array* keys)
{
    // Forward enter so the game's keyboard state stays consistent; individual
    // keys are withheld in wk_key while the pointer is over the overlay.
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(gameDataMutex);
    auto it = gameKeyboards.find(kb);
    if (it != gameKeyboards.end() && it->second.original.enter)
        it->second.original.enter(it->second.userData, kb, serial, s, keys);
}

static void wk_leave(void* data, wl_keyboard* kb, uint32_t serial, wl_surface* s)
{
    // Always forward leave
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(gameDataMutex);
    auto it = gameKeyboards.find(kb);
    if (it != gameKeyboards.end() && it->second.original.leave)
        it->second.original.leave(it->second.userData, kb, serial, s);
}

static void wk_key(void* data, wl_keyboard* kb, uint32_t serial, uint32_t time, uint32_t key, uint32_t state)
{
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(gameDataMutex);
        std::unordered_set<uint32_t>& held = gameHeldKeys[kb];
        if (state == WL_KEYBOARD_KEY_STATE_PRESSED)
            held.insert(key);
        else
            held.erase(key);
    }

    // keys follow the pointer hitbox plus the overlay's own key consumption
    if (pointerBlocked() || VkHook::isOverlayConsumingKeys())
        return;
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(gameDataMutex);
    auto it = gameKeyboards.find(kb);
    if (it != gameKeyboards.end() && it->second.original.key)
        it->second.original.key(it->second.userData, kb, serial, time, key, state);
}

static void wk_modifiers(void* data, wl_keyboard* kb, uint32_t serial, uint32_t depressed, uint32_t latched, uint32_t locked, uint32_t group)
{
    // Always forward modifiers — games need modifier state for keybinds
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(gameDataMutex);
    auto it = gameKeyboards.find(kb);
    if (it != gameKeyboards.end() && it->second.original.modifiers)
        it->second.original.modifiers(it->second.userData, kb, serial, depressed, latched, locked, group);
}

static void wk_repeat_info(void* data, wl_keyboard* kb, int32_t rate, int32_t delay)
{
    // Always forward repeat info
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(gameDataMutex);
    auto it = gameKeyboards.find(kb);
    if (it != gameKeyboards.end() && it->second.original.repeat_info)
        it->second.original.repeat_info(it->second.userData, kb, rate, delay);
}

static const wl_keyboard_listener wrapperKeyboardListener = {
    .keymap = wk_keymap,
    .enter = wk_enter,
    .leave = wk_leave,
    .key = wk_key,
    .modifiers = wk_modifiers,
    .repeat_info = wk_repeat_info,
};

// ── Wrapper dispatcher callbacks ────────────────────────────────────────────

static int wd_pointer(const void* data, void* target, uint32_t opcode, const struct wl_message* msg, union wl_argument* args)
{
    auto* proxy = static_cast<wl_proxy*>(target);

    // enter/motion carry surface coords; remember the latest for the events
    // that do not (button, axis, frame).
    if (opcode == 0) // enter: serial, surface, x, y
    {
        g_lastPointerX.store(wl_fixed_to_double(args[2].f), std::memory_order_release);
        g_lastPointerY.store(wl_fixed_to_double(args[3].f), std::memory_order_release);
    }
    else if (opcode == 2) // motion: time, x, y
    {
        g_lastPointerX.store(wl_fixed_to_double(args[1].f), std::memory_order_release);
        g_lastPointerY.store(wl_fixed_to_double(args[2].f), std::memory_order_release);
    }

    if (opcode == 3 && VkHook::isWayland())
        VkHook::mirrorButtonState(args[2].u, args[3].u == WL_POINTER_BUTTON_STATE_PRESSED);

    // forward enter/leave so the game tracks the pointer, withhold everything
    // positional while it sits over the overlay.
    if (opcode >= 2 && opcode <= 10 && pointerBlocked())
        return 0;

    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(gameDataMutex);
    auto it = gamePointerDispatchers.find(proxy);
    if (it != gamePointerDispatchers.end() && it->second.original)
        return it->second.original(it->second.dispatcherData, target, opcode, msg, args);
    return 0;
}

static int wd_keyboard(const void* data, void* target, uint32_t opcode, const struct wl_message* msg, union wl_argument* args)
{
    auto* proxy = static_cast<wl_proxy*>(target);

    if (opcode == 3) // key: serial, time, key, state
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(gameDataMutex);
        std::unordered_set<uint32_t>& held = gameHeldKeys[(wl_keyboard*)proxy];
        if (args[3].u == WL_KEYBOARD_KEY_STATE_PRESSED)
            held.insert(args[2].u);
        else
            held.erase(args[2].u);
    }

    // keyboard has no coordinates; it follows the hitbox and the overlay's
    // own key consumption
    if (opcode == 3 && (pointerBlocked() || VkHook::isOverlayConsumingKeys()))
        return 0;

    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(gameDataMutex);
    auto it = gameKeyboardDispatchers.find(proxy);
    if (it != gameKeyboardDispatchers.end() && it->second.original)
        return it->second.original(it->second.dispatcherData, target, opcode, msg, args);
    return 0;
}

// ── Symbol interposition ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// wl_pointer_add_listener is a static inline in <wayland-client-protocol.h>
// that calls wl_proxy_add_listener. We interpose on the underlying C function
// so that even inlined calls are caught.

using AddListenerFn = int (*)(struct wl_proxy*, void (**)(void), void*);
using DlsymFn = void* (*)(void*, const char*);

static DlsymFn getRealDlsym()
{
    static DlsymFn fn = nullptr;
    if (fn)
        return fn;

    // Prefer a versioned lookup to avoid self-recursion when we interpose dlsym.
    fn = reinterpret_cast<DlsymFn>(dlvsym(RTLD_NEXT, "dlsym", "GLIBC_2.2.5"));
    if (!fn)
        fn = reinterpret_cast<DlsymFn>(dlvsym(RTLD_NEXT, "dlsym", "GLIBC_2.34"));
    return fn;
}

template <typename FnType>
static FnType resolveWaylandSymbol(const char* symbol)
{
    DlsymFn realDlsym = getRealDlsym();
    if (!realDlsym)
        return nullptr;

    // Preferred path for normal implicit-layer usage.
    void* sym = realDlsym(RTLD_NEXT, symbol);
    if (sym)
        return reinterpret_cast<FnType>(sym);

    // Fallback for preload / early-load scenarios where RTLD_NEXT may not
    // reach libwayland-client yet.
    static void* waylandHandle = nullptr;
    if (!waylandHandle)
    {
        waylandHandle = dlopen("libwayland-client.so.0", RTLD_NOLOAD | RTLD_NOW);
        if (!waylandHandle)
            waylandHandle = dlopen("libwayland-client.so.0", RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL);
    }

    if (waylandHandle)
    {
        sym = realDlsym(waylandHandle, symbol);
        if (sym)
            return reinterpret_cast<FnType>(sym);
    }

    return nullptr;
}

static AddListenerFn getRealAddListener()
{
    static AddListenerFn fn = resolveWaylandSymbol<AddListenerFn>("wl_proxy_add_listener");
    return fn;
}

using AddDispatcherFn = int (*)(struct wl_proxy*, wl_dispatcher_func_t, const void*, void*);
using MarshalArrayFlagsFn = wl_proxy* (*)(struct wl_proxy*, uint32_t, const struct wl_interface*, uint32_t, uint32_t, union wl_argument*);

static AddDispatcherFn getRealAddDispatcher()
{
    static AddDispatcherFn fn = resolveWaylandSymbol<AddDispatcherFn>("wl_proxy_add_dispatcher");
    return fn;
}

static MarshalArrayFlagsFn getRealMarshalArrayFlags(void* caller)
{
    // the installer records the real entry of every gated libwayland copy;
    // pick the copy the caller lives in
    if (void* gated = VkHook::waylandMarshalArrayFlagsForCaller(caller))
        return reinterpret_cast<MarshalArrayFlagsFn>(gated);

    // not gated (e.g. reached through symbol interposition): fall back to a
    // handle-scoped lookup, which can never recurse into this wrapper
    static std::atomic<MarshalArrayFlagsFn> fallback{nullptr};
    MarshalArrayFlagsFn fn = fallback.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
    if (fn)
        return fn;

    static void* waylandHandle = nullptr;
    if (!waylandHandle)
        waylandHandle = dlopen("libwayland-client.so.0", RTLD_NOLOAD | RTLD_NOW);
    if (!waylandHandle)
        waylandHandle = dlopen("libwayland-client.so.0", RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL);
    if (DlsymFn real = getRealDlsym(); waylandHandle && real)
        fn = reinterpret_cast<MarshalArrayFlagsFn>(real(waylandHandle, "wl_proxy_marshal_array_flags"));

    if (fn)
        fallback.store(fn, std::memory_order_release);
    return fn;
}

extern "C" __attribute__((visibility("default")))
int wl_proxy_add_listener(struct wl_proxy* proxy,
                          void (**implementation)(void),
                          void* data)
{
    AddListenerFn real = getRealAddListener();
    if (!real)
        return -1;

    const char* cls = wl_proxy_get_class(proxy);
    if (!cls)
        return real(proxy, implementation, data);

    // Skip overlay-owned proxies — they use their own listeners
    if (VkHook::isOverlayProxy(proxy))
        return real(proxy, implementation, data);

    if (std::strcmp(cls, "wl_pointer") == 0)
    {
        auto* gameListener = (const wl_pointer_listener*)implementation;
        auto* ptr = (wl_pointer*)proxy;

        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(gameDataMutex);
            GamePointerData gpd;
            gpd.original = *gameListener;
            gpd.userData = data;
            gamePointers[ptr] = gpd;
        }

        VkHook::Logger::debug("Wayland interpose: wrapped game pointer listener");
        return real(proxy, (void (**)(void))&wrapperPointerListener, nullptr);
    }

    if (std::strcmp(cls, "wl_keyboard") == 0)
    {
        auto* gameListener = (const wl_keyboard_listener*)implementation;
        auto* kb = (wl_keyboard*)proxy;

        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(gameDataMutex);
            GameKeyboardData gkd;
            gkd.original = *gameListener;
            gkd.userData = data;
            gameKeyboards[kb] = gkd;
        }

        VkHook::Logger::debug("Wayland interpose: wrapped game keyboard listener");
        return real(proxy, (void (**)(void))&wrapperKeyboardListener, nullptr);
    }

    return real(proxy, implementation, data);
}

extern "C" __attribute__((visibility("default")))
int wl_proxy_add_dispatcher(struct wl_proxy* proxy,
                            wl_dispatcher_func_t dispatcher_func,
                            const void* dispatcher_data,
                            void* data);

extern "C" __attribute__((visibility("default")))
wl_proxy* wl_proxy_marshal_array_flags(struct wl_proxy* proxy,
                                       uint32_t opcode,
                                       const struct wl_interface* iface,
                                       uint32_t version,
                                       uint32_t flags,
                                       union wl_argument* args)
{
    MarshalArrayFlagsFn real = getRealMarshalArrayFlags(__builtin_return_address(0));
    if (!real)
        return nullptr;

    // hold window commits while Mesa's present may have explicit-sync points
    // in flight on this surface (see wayland_syncobj_gate.hh); outside a
    // present the gate is closed and this whole block is one atomic load
    if (opcode == 6 && VkHook::WaylandSyncobjGate::anyPresentOpen())
    {
        const char* cls = wl_proxy_get_class(proxy);
        if (cls && std::strcmp(cls, "wl_surface") == 0)
            VkHook::WaylandSyncobjGate::beginCommit(wl_proxy_get_id(proxy));
    }

    return real(proxy, opcode, iface, version, flags, args);
}

extern "C" __attribute__((visibility("default")))
void* dlsym(void* handle, const char* symbol)
{
    DlsymFn realDlsym = getRealDlsym();
    if (!realDlsym)
        return nullptr;

    void* resolved = realDlsym(handle, symbol);

    // Keep behavior unchanged unless VkHook is explicitly enabled.
    // Cache the check — this function is called for every dlsym in the process.
    static const bool VkHookEnabled = []{
        const char* e = std::getenv("ENABLE_VKHOOK");
        return e && std::strcmp(e, "1") == 0;
    }();
    if (!VkHookEnabled || !resolved)
        return resolved;

    bool wantsListener = (std::strcmp(symbol, "wl_proxy_add_listener") == 0);
    bool wantsDispatcher = (std::strcmp(symbol, "wl_proxy_add_dispatcher") == 0);
    bool wantsMarshalArrayFlags = (std::strcmp(symbol, "wl_proxy_marshal_array_flags") == 0);
    if (!wantsListener && !wantsDispatcher && !wantsMarshalArrayFlags)
        return resolved;

    Dl_info info{};
    if (dladdr(resolved, &info) == 0 || !info.dli_fname)
        return resolved;

    std::string module(info.dli_fname);
    std::transform(module.begin(), module.end(), module.begin(),
                   [](unsigned char c) { return static_cast<char>(std::tolower(c)); });

    // Only redirect lookups that currently resolve to libwayland-client.
    if (module.find("libwayland-client") == std::string::npos)
    {
        return resolved;
    }

    if (wantsListener)
        return reinterpret_cast<void*>(&wl_proxy_add_listener);
    if (wantsDispatcher)
        return reinterpret_cast<void*>(&wl_proxy_add_dispatcher);
    return reinterpret_cast<void*>(&wl_proxy_marshal_array_flags);
}

extern "C" __attribute__((visibility("default")))
int wl_proxy_add_dispatcher(struct wl_proxy* proxy,
                            wl_dispatcher_func_t dispatcher_func,
                            const void* dispatcher_data,
                            void* data)
{
    AddDispatcherFn real = getRealAddDispatcher();
    if (!real)
        return -1;

    const char* cls = wl_proxy_get_class(proxy);
    if (!cls)
        return real(proxy, dispatcher_func, dispatcher_data, data);

    // Skip overlay-owned proxies — they use their own dispatchers
    if (VkHook::isOverlayProxy(proxy))
        return real(proxy, dispatcher_func, dispatcher_data, data);

    if (std::strcmp(cls, "wl_pointer") == 0)
    {
        auto* ptr = static_cast<wl_proxy*>(proxy);

        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(gameDataMutex);
            GamePointerDispatcherData gpd;
            gpd.original = dispatcher_func;
            gpd.dispatcherData = dispatcher_data;
            gamePointerDispatchers[ptr] = gpd;
        }

        VkHook::Logger::debug("Wayland interpose: wrapped game pointer dispatcher");
        return real(proxy, wd_pointer, nullptr, data);
    }

    if (std::strcmp(cls, "wl_keyboard") == 0)
    {
        auto* kb = static_cast<wl_proxy*>(proxy);

        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(gameDataMutex);
            GameKeyboardDispatcherData gkd;
            gkd.original = dispatcher_func;
            gkd.dispatcherData = dispatcher_data;
            gameKeyboardDispatchers[kb] = gkd;
        }

        VkHook::Logger::debug("Wayland interpose: wrapped game keyboard dispatcher");
        return real(proxy, wd_keyboard, nullptr, data);
    }

    return real(proxy, dispatcher_func, dispatcher_data, data);
}

namespace VkHook
{
    void withholdGameKeys(bool withhold)
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(gameDataMutex);

        size_t changed = 0;
        const uint32_t state = withhold ? WL_KEYBOARD_KEY_STATE_RELEASED : WL_KEYBOARD_KEY_STATE_PRESSED;

        for (auto& [kb, data] : gameKeyboards)
        {
            auto heldIt = gameHeldKeys.find(kb);
            if (heldIt == gameHeldKeys.end())
                continue;
            for (uint32_t key : heldIt->second)
            {
                if (data.original.key)
                    data.original.key(data.userData, kb, 0, 0, key, state);
                changed++;
            }
        }

        for (auto& [proxy, data] : gameKeyboardDispatchers)
        {
            auto heldIt = gameHeldKeys.find((wl_keyboard*)proxy);
            if (heldIt == gameHeldKeys.end() || !data.original)
                continue;
            for (uint32_t key : heldIt->second)
            {
                union wl_argument args[4] = {};
                args[0].u = 0; // serial
                args[1].u = 0; // time
                args[2].u = key;
                args[3].u = state;
                data.original(data.dispatcherData, proxy, 3, &wl_keyboard_interface.events[3], args);
                changed++;
            }
        }

        if (changed > 0)
            Logger::debug(std::string("Wayland interpose: ") + (withhold ? "released " : "re-pressed ")
                          + std::to_string(changed) + " held game key(s)");
    }
} // namespace VkHook

namespace VkHook::WaylandSyncobjGate
{
    uint32_t waylandSurfaceId()
    {
        if (!VkHook::isWayland())
            return 0;

        wl_surface* surface = VkHook::getWaylandSurface();
        return surface ? wl_proxy_get_id(reinterpret_cast<struct wl_proxy*>(surface)) : 0;
    }
} // namespace VkHook::WaylandSyncobjGate
```

```hh
#pragma once

struct wl_proxy;

namespace VkHook
{
    // Register overlay-owned proxies so the interposition layer skips them.
    // Call BEFORE wl_pointer_add_listener / wl_keyboard_add_listener.
    void registerOverlayProxy(wl_proxy* proxy);
    void unregisterOverlayProxy(wl_proxy* proxy);

    // Release every key the wrapped game keyboards currently hold (or re-press
    // whatever is still physically held). Called when the pointer crosses the
    // overlay hitbox, so a held movement key stops without dropping keyboard
    // focus — a synthetic leave/enter stalls input until the next press.
    // Mouse buttons are deliberately untouched: a synthetic release would break
    // click/drag ordering. Only works when the listener/dispatcher interposition
    // is active.
    void withholdGameKeys(bool withhold);
}
```

`src/input/wayland_interpose_patch.cc`:

```cc
#include "wayland_interpose_patch.hh"

#include "logger.hh"

#include <wayland-client.h>

#include <dlfcn.h>
#include <elf.h>
#include <link.h>
#include <sys/mman.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#include <atomic>
#include <chrono>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstring>
#include <mutex>
#include <string>

namespace
{
    constexpr int kMaxCopies = 8;

    struct PatchedCopy
    {
        uintptr_t lo;
        uintptr_t hi;
        void* real;
    };

    PatchedCopy g_copies[kMaxCopies];
    std::atomic<int> g_copyCount{0};
    std::mutex g_installMutex;
    std::atomic<int64_t> g_lastScanNs{0};

    bool nameMatches(const char* path, const char* needle)
    {
        return path && std::strstr(path, needle) != nullptr;
    }

    // glibc rewrites DT_SYMTAB/DT_STRTAB/DT_JMPREL values in place to absolute
    // addresses at load time; a rare configuration leaves them relative.
    // Accept both; the caller validates the resulting address against PT_LOAD.
    uintptr_t normalize(uintptr_t base, uintptr_t value)
    {
        if (value < base)
            return value <= UINTPTR_MAX - base ? base + value : 0;
        return value;
    }

    // restore the protection the page had before we touched it, read straight
    // from /proc/self/maps (RELRO got pages are read-only)
    void restoreProtection(uintptr_t pageAddr, size_t pageSize)
    {
        int flags = PROT_READ;
        if (FILE* maps = std::fopen("/proc/self/maps", "re"))
        {
            char line[512];
            while (std::fgets(line, sizeof(line), maps))
            {
                unsigned long start = 0;
                unsigned long end = 0;
                char perms[8] = {0};
                if (std::sscanf(line, "%lx-%lx %7s", &start, &end, perms) == 3 && start <= pageAddr && pageAddr < end)
                {
                    flags = 0;
                    if (perms[0] == 'r') flags |= PROT_READ;
                    if (perms[1] == 'w') flags |= PROT_WRITE;
                    if (perms[2] == 'x') flags |= PROT_EXEC;
                    if (flags == 0)
                        flags = PROT_READ;
                    break;
                }
            }
            std::fclose(maps);
        }
        mprotect(reinterpret_cast<void*>(pageAddr), pageSize, flags);
    }

    struct Scan
    {
        const char* symbol;
        void* replacement;
        bool probeOnly;
        bool stopped;
        void** foundSlot;
        void** foundReal;
    };

    void tryPatchObject(struct dl_phdr_info* info, Scan& scan)
    {
        const uintptr_t base = static_cast<uintptr_t>(info->dlpi_addr);

        // already gated? (same base means same load)
        const int known = g_copyCount.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
        for (int i = 0; i < known; ++i)
        {
            if (g_copies[i].lo == base)
                return;
        }

        // object load ranges + dynamic segment
        uintptr_t lo = UINTPTR_MAX;
        uintptr_t hi = 0;
        const ElfW(Phdr)* dynPhdr = nullptr;
        for (ElfW(Half) i = 0; i < info->dlpi_phnum; ++i)
        {
            const ElfW(Phdr)& ph = info->dlpi_phdr[i];
            if (ph.p_type == PT_LOAD && ph.p_memsz)
            {
                if (ph.p_vaddr > UINTPTR_MAX - base)
                    return;
                const uintptr_t segLo = base + static_cast<uintptr_t>(ph.p_vaddr);
                if (ph.p_memsz > UINTPTR_MAX - segLo)
                    return;
                const uintptr_t segHi = segLo + static_cast<uintptr_t>(ph.p_memsz);
                lo = segLo < lo ? segLo : lo;
                hi = segHi > hi ? segHi : hi;
            }
            else if (ph.p_type == PT_DYNAMIC)
            {
                dynPhdr = &ph;
            }
        }
        if (!dynPhdr || lo >= hi)
            return;

        auto inRange = [&](uintptr_t p, size_t len) {
            if (p < lo || len > hi - lo || p > hi - len)
                return false;
            // The envelope can contain unmapped gaps between load segments.
            for (ElfW(Half) i = 0; i < info->dlpi_phnum; ++i)
            {
                const ElfW(Phdr)& ph = info->dlpi_phdr[i];
                if (ph.p_type != PT_LOAD || !ph.p_memsz || !(ph.p_flags & PF_R))
                    continue;
                const uintptr_t start = base + static_cast<uintptr_t>(ph.p_vaddr);
                if (p >= start && len <= ph.p_memsz && p - start <= ph.p_memsz - len)
                    return true;
            }
            return false;
        };
        auto ptrIn = [&](const void* p, size_t len) {
            return inRange(reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(p), len);
        };

        if (dynPhdr->p_vaddr > UINTPTR_MAX - base)
            return;
        const auto* dynamic = reinterpret_cast<const ElfW(Dyn)*>(base + static_cast<uintptr_t>(dynPhdr->p_vaddr));
        if (!ptrIn(dynamic, dynPhdr->p_memsz))
            return;

        const ElfW(Sym)* symtab = nullptr;
        const char* strtab = nullptr;
        const void* jmprel = nullptr;
        const ElfW(Rel)* rels = nullptr;
        const ElfW(Rela)* relas = nullptr;
        size_t strsz = 0;
        size_t pltrelsz = 0;
        size_t relsz = 0;
        size_t relasz = 0;
        size_t relent = 0;
        size_t relaent = 0;
        ElfW(Xword) pltrel = DT_NULL;
        bool terminated = false;
        const size_t dynamicCount = dynPhdr->p_memsz / sizeof(ElfW(Dyn));
        for (size_t i = 0; i < dynamicCount; ++i)
        {
            const ElfW(Dyn)& dyn = dynamic[i];
            if (dyn.d_tag == DT_NULL)
            {
                terminated = true;
                break;
            }
            switch (dyn.d_tag)
            {
                case DT_SYMTAB: symtab = reinterpret_cast<const ElfW(Sym)*>(normalize(base, dyn.d_un.d_ptr)); break;
                case DT_STRTAB: strtab = reinterpret_cast<const char*>(normalize(base, dyn.d_un.d_ptr)); break;
                case DT_STRSZ: strsz = static_cast<size_t>(dyn.d_un.d_val); break;
                case DT_JMPREL: jmprel = reinterpret_cast<const void*>(normalize(base, dyn.d_un.d_ptr)); break;
                case DT_PLTRELSZ: pltrelsz = static_cast<size_t>(dyn.d_un.d_val); break;
                case DT_PLTREL: pltrel = dyn.d_un.d_val; break;
                case DT_REL: rels = reinterpret_cast<const ElfW(Rel)*>(normalize(base, dyn.d_un.d_ptr)); break;
                case DT_RELSZ: relsz = static_cast<size_t>(dyn.d_un.d_val); break;
                case DT_RELENT: relent = static_cast<size_t>(dyn.d_un.d_val); break;
                case DT_RELA: relas = reinterpret_cast<const ElfW(Rela)*>(normalize(base, dyn.d_un.d_ptr)); break;
                case DT_RELASZ: relasz = static_cast<size_t>(dyn.d_un.d_val); break;
                case DT_RELAENT: relaent = static_cast<size_t>(dyn.d_un.d_val); break;
                default: break;
            }
        }

        if (!terminated || !symtab || !strtab || strsz == 0 ||
            !ptrIn(symtab, sizeof(ElfW(Sym))) || !ptrIn(strtab, strsz))
            return;

        // dl_iterate_phdr exposes only the process's native ELF class. i386
        // normally uses REL and x86_64 RELA; DT_PLTREL, not the CPU, selects
        // the actual PLT entry layout.
#if defined(__i386__)
        constexpr unsigned jumpSlotType = R_386_JMP_SLOT;
        constexpr unsigned globalDataType = R_386_GLOB_DAT;
#elif defined(__x86_64__) && UINTPTR_MAX == UINT64_MAX
        constexpr unsigned jumpSlotType = R_X86_64_JUMP_SLOT;
        constexpr unsigned globalDataType = R_X86_64_GLOB_DAT;
#else
#error "Wayland GOT interposition requires i386 or x86_64 ELF"
#endif

        const size_t wanted = std::strlen(scan.symbol);
        auto scanRelocations = [&](const auto* relocations, size_t bytes, unsigned slotType) {
            const size_t entrySize = sizeof(*relocations);
            const size_t count = bytes / entrySize;
            if (!relocations || bytes % entrySize != 0 || count == 0 ||
                count > 65536 || !ptrIn(relocations, bytes))
                return false;

            for (size_t i = 0; i < count; ++i)
            {
                const auto& rel = relocations[i];
#if defined(__i386__)
                const unsigned type = ELF32_R_TYPE(rel.r_info);
                const size_t symbolIndex = ELF32_R_SYM(rel.r_info);
#else
                const unsigned type = ELF64_R_TYPE(rel.r_info);
                const size_t symbolIndex = ELF64_R_SYM(rel.r_info);
#endif
                if (type != slotType)
                    continue;

                const uintptr_t symtabAddr = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(symtab);
                if (symbolIndex > (hi - symtabAddr) / sizeof(ElfW(Sym)))
                    continue;
                const auto* sym = reinterpret_cast<const ElfW(Sym)*>(symtabAddr + symbolIndex * sizeof(ElfW(Sym)));
                if (!ptrIn(sym, sizeof(ElfW(Sym))) || sym->st_name >= strsz ||
                    wanted >= strsz - sym->st_name)
                    continue;

                const char* name = strtab + sym->st_name;
                if (std::memcmp(name, scan.symbol, wanted) != 0 || name[wanted] != '\0')
                    continue;

                if (rel.r_offset > UINTPTR_MAX - base)
                    continue;
                const uintptr_t slotAddr = base + static_cast<uintptr_t>(rel.r_offset);
                if (slotAddr % alignof(void*) != 0 ||
                    !ptrIn(reinterpret_cast<const void*>(slotAddr), sizeof(void*)))
                    continue;

                auto* slot = reinterpret_cast<void**>(slotAddr);
                void* current = *slot;

                // Only gate a resolved entry into this copy of libwayland.
                // A lazy PLT stub also belongs to this object, so require the
                // actual symbol address rather than just a matching load base.
                Dl_info resolved{};
                if (sym->st_shndx == SHN_UNDEF || sym->st_value > UINTPTR_MAX - base ||
                    reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(current) != base + sym->st_value ||
                    dladdr(current, &resolved) == 0 ||
                    reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(resolved.dli_fbase) != base)
                    continue;

                if (scan.probeOnly)
                {
                    if (scan.foundSlot)
                        *scan.foundSlot = slot;
                    if (scan.foundReal)
                        *scan.foundReal = current;
                    scan.stopped = true;
                    return true;
                }

                const int index = g_copyCount.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
                if (index >= kMaxCopies)
                    return true;

                const long pageSizeLong = sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE);
                const size_t pageSize = pageSizeLong > 0 ? static_cast<size_t>(pageSizeLong) : 4096;
                const uintptr_t pageAddr = slotAddr & ~static_cast<uintptr_t>(pageSize - 1);
                if (mprotect(reinterpret_cast<void*>(pageAddr), pageSize, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE) != 0)
                    return true;

                // publish the real entry before any thread can reach the patched slot
                g_copies[index] = {lo, hi, current};
                g_copyCount.store(index + 1, std::memory_order_release);
                *slot = scan.replacement;

                restoreProtection(pageAddr, pageSize);

                VkHook::Logger::info("Wayland interpose: gated the marshal entry in " + std::string(info->dlpi_name));
                return true;
            }
            return false;
        };

        if (pltrel == DT_REL &&
            scanRelocations(static_cast<const ElfW(Rel)*>(jmprel), pltrelsz, jumpSlotType))
            return;
        if (pltrel == DT_RELA &&
            scanRelocations(static_cast<const ElfW(Rela)*>(jmprel), pltrelsz, jumpSlotType))
            return;

        // -fno-plt builds call through GLOB_DAT GOT entries instead of JUMP_SLOT.
        if (relent == sizeof(ElfW(Rel)) && scanRelocations(rels, relsz, globalDataType))
            return;
        if (relaent == sizeof(ElfW(Rela)))
            scanRelocations(relas, relasz, globalDataType);
    }

    int scanCallback(struct dl_phdr_info* info, size_t, void* data)
    {
        auto* scan = static_cast<Scan*>(data);
        if (nameMatches(info->dlpi_name, "libwayland-client.so"))
            tryPatchObject(info, *scan);
        return scan->stopped ? 1 : 0;
    }
} // namespace

namespace VkHook
{
    void* waylandMarshalArrayFlagsForCaller(void* caller)
    {
        const uintptr_t pc = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(caller);
        const int count = g_copyCount.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
        for (int i = 0; i < count; ++i)
        {
            if (pc >= g_copies[i].lo && pc < g_copies[i].hi)
                return g_copies[i].real;
        }
        return count > 0 ? g_copies[0].real : nullptr;
    }

    void installWaylandInterposeHooks()
    {
        // called before every present to catch libwayland copies that load
        // after us; scanning walks every loaded object, so keep it to a
        // once-a-second cadence instead of once a frame
        const int64_t now = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(
                                std::chrono::steady_clock::now().time_since_epoch())
                                .count();
        int64_t last = g_lastScanNs.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
        if (last != 0 && now - last < 1'000'000'000LL)
            return;
        if (!g_lastScanNs.compare_exchange_strong(last, now, std::memory_order_relaxed))
            return;

        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(g_installMutex);
        Scan scan{"wl_proxy_marshal_array_flags",
                  reinterpret_cast<void*>(&wl_proxy_marshal_array_flags),
                  false, false, nullptr, nullptr};
        dl_iterate_phdr(scanCallback, &scan);
    }

    bool waylandMarshalSlotForTests(void** slotOut, void** realOut)
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(g_installMutex);
        Scan scan{"wl_proxy_marshal_array_flags", nullptr, true, false, slotOut, realOut};
        dl_iterate_phdr(scanCallback, &scan);
        return scan.stopped;
    }
} // namespace VkHook
```

`src/input/wayland_interpose_patch.hh`:

```hh
#pragma once

namespace VkHook
{
    // Redirect libwayland's internal marshal entry (the jump slot behind
    // wl_proxy_marshal_flags) at our array-flags wrapper so every caller's
    // requests cross the explicit-sync gate. Idempotent and crash-safe:
    // every address read out of an object's dynamic section is validated
    // against that object's own load ranges before use. Retried on later
    // calls so copies of libwayland that load after us are gated too.
    void installWaylandInterposeHooks();

    // The real marshal entry of the libwayland copy the given caller lives
    // in, or null when nothing has been gated yet.
    void* waylandMarshalArrayFlagsForCaller(void* caller);

    // Test hook: locate the jump slot without redirecting it. Returns false
    // when no loaded object carries the relocation.
    bool waylandMarshalSlotForTests(void** slotOut, void** realOut);
} // namespace VkHook
```

`src/input/wayland_pointer_constraints.cc`:

```cc
#include "wayland_pointer_constraints.hh"
#include "wayland_display.hh"
#include "wayland_input_common.hh"
#include "logger.hh"

#include <wayland-client.h>
#include "pointer-constraints-unstable-v1-client-protocol.h"

#include <cstring>

namespace VkHook
{
    static zwp_pointer_constraints_v1* constraints = nullptr;
    static zwp_confined_pointer_v1* confinedPointer = nullptr;
    static wl_pointer* pointer = nullptr;
    static bool constraintsInitialized = false;

    // Confined pointer listener
    static void confinedPointerConfined(void* /*data*/, zwp_confined_pointer_v1* /*cp*/)
    {
        Logger::debug("Wayland: pointer confined to surface");
    }

    static void confinedPointerUnconfined(void* /*data*/, zwp_confined_pointer_v1* /*cp*/)
    {
        Logger::debug("Wayland: pointer unconfined");
    }

    static const zwp_confined_pointer_v1_listener confinedPointerListener = {
        .confined = confinedPointerConfined,
        .unconfined = confinedPointerUnconfined,
    };

    // Registry listener to bind pointer constraints global
    static void constraintsRegistryGlobal(void* /*data*/, wl_registry* reg,
                                          uint32_t name, const char* interface, uint32_t version)
    {
        if (std::strcmp(interface, zwp_pointer_constraints_v1_interface.name) != 0)
            return;
        if (constraints)
            return;

        constraints = (zwp_pointer_constraints_v1*)wl_registry_bind(
            reg, name, &zwp_pointer_constraints_v1_interface,
            version < 1 ? version : 1);
        Logger::debug("Wayland: pointer constraints bound");
    }

    static void constraintsRegistryGlobalRemove(void* /*data*/, wl_registry* /*reg*/, uint32_t /*name*/)
    {
    }

    static const wl_registry_listener constraintsRegistryListener = {
        .global = constraintsRegistryGlobal,
        .global_remove = constraintsRegistryGlobalRemove,
    };

    bool initPointerConstraints()
    {
        if (constraintsInitialized)
            return constraints != nullptr;

        wl_display* display = getWaylandDisplay();
        if (!display)
            return false;

        // Ensure shared input is initialized first (creates the event queue)
        if (!initWaylandInputCommon())
            return false;

        constraintsInitialized = true;

        // We need our own registry query on the shared queue to find the
        // pointer constraints global. The shared input common registry
        // only looks for wl_seat.
        wl_display* wrapper = (wl_display*)wl_proxy_create_wrapper(display);
        if (!wrapper)
            return false;

        wl_event_queue* q = getWaylandInputQueue();
        if (!q)
        {
            wl_proxy_wrapper_destroy(wrapper);
            return false;
        }

        wl_proxy_set_queue((wl_proxy*)wrapper, q);

        wl_registry* reg = wl_display_get_registry(wrapper);
        wl_registry_add_listener(reg, &constraintsRegistryListener, nullptr);

        wl_display_roundtrip_queue(display, q);

        wl_registry_destroy(reg);
        wl_proxy_wrapper_destroy(wrapper);

        if (constraints)
            Logger::info("Wayland: pointer constraints initialized");
        else
            Logger::info("Wayland: pointer constraints not available (compositor may not support zwp_pointer_constraints_v1)");

        return constraints != nullptr;
    }

    void confinePointer()
    {
        if (!constraints)
        {
            if (!initPointerConstraints())
                return;
        }

        if (confinedPointer)
        {
            Logger::debug("Wayland: pointer already confined, skipping");
            return;
        }

        wl_surface* surface = getWaylandSurface();
        if (!surface)
        {
            Logger::debug("Wayland: no surface available for pointer confinement");
            return;
        }

        // Get a pointer from the seat for confinement. We get our own
        // because the mouse_input module's pointer is private.
        if (!pointer)
        {
            if (!initWaylandInputCommon())
            {
                Logger::debug("Wayland: cannot confine pointer — no seat available");
                return;
            }

            // The pointer bind callback is already claimed by mouse_input,
            // so we get our own wl_pointer from the seat directly.
            // This is safe because wl_seat_get_pointer returns a new proxy
            // each time — we just won't add a listener (we don't need events).
            wl_seat* seat = getWaylandSeat();
            if (!seat)
            {
                Logger::debug("Wayland: cannot confine pointer — seat not available");
                return;
            }
            pointer = wl_seat_get_pointer(seat);
            if (!pointer)
            {
                Logger::debug("Wayland: cannot confine pointer — seat has no pointer capability");
                return;
            }
            Logger::debug("Wayland: obtained pointer from seat for confinement");
        }

        confinedPointer = zwp_pointer_constraints_v1_confine_pointer(
            constraints, surface, pointer, nullptr,
            ZWP_POINTER_CONSTRAINTS_V1_LIFETIME_PERSISTENT);

        if (!confinedPointer)
        {
            // The compositor may return NULL if the surface already has a
            // constraint (e.g., the game locked the pointer). This is not fatal.
            Logger::debug("Wayland: confine_pointer returned NULL — surface may already be constrained");
            return;
        }

        zwp_confined_pointer_v1_add_listener(confinedPointer, &confinedPointerListener, nullptr);

        // Flush to apply immediately
        wl_display* display = getWaylandDisplay();
        if (display)
            wl_display_flush(display);

        Logger::debug("Wayland: pointer confinement requested");
    }

    void releasePointer()
    {
        if (!confinedPointer)
            return;

        zwp_confined_pointer_v1_destroy(confinedPointer);
        confinedPointer = nullptr;

        // Flush to apply immediately
        wl_display* display = getWaylandDisplay();
        if (display)
            wl_display_flush(display);

        Logger::debug("Wayland: pointer confinement released");
    }

    void cleanupPointerConstraints()
    {
        releasePointer();

        if (pointer)
        {
            wl_pointer_destroy(pointer);
            pointer = nullptr;
        }

        if (constraints)
        {
            zwp_pointer_constraints_v1_destroy(constraints);
            constraints = nullptr;
        }

        constraintsInitialized = false;
    }

} // namespace VkHook

```

```hh
#pragma once

namespace VkHook
{
    // Initialize pointer constraints from the Wayland registry.
    // Requires initWaylandInputCommon() to have been called first.
    bool initPointerConstraints();

    // Confine the pointer to the game's wl_surface (entire surface).
    // No-op if already confined or if constraints aren't available.
    void confinePointer();

    // Release the pointer confinement.
    // No-op if not currently confined.
    void releasePointer();

    // Clean up pointer constraints resources.
    void cleanupPointerConstraints();
```

`src/input/wayland_syncobj_gate.cc`:

```cc
#include "wayland_syncobj_gate.hh"

#include "logger.hh"

#include <atomic>
#include <chrono>
#include <condition_variable>
#include <mutex>
#include <thread>
#include <unordered_map>

namespace VkHook::WaylandSyncobjGate
{
    namespace
    {
        using Clock = std::chrono::steady_clock;

        std::mutex mutex;
        std::condition_variable cv;

        // surface id -> the presenting thread, while it is inside the driver
        std::unordered_map<uint32_t, std::thread::id> openPresents;

        std::atomic<bool> anyOpen{false};
        std::atomic<uint64_t> held{0};
        std::atomic<uint64_t> budgetMicros{100'000};

        // waits out another thread's present; true if it actually waited
        bool waitForCloseLocked(std::unique_lock<std::mutex>& lock, uint32_t surfaceId)
        {
            const auto deadline = Clock::now() + std::chrono::microseconds(budgetMicros.load(std::memory_order_relaxed));
            bool waited = false;

            while (true)
            {
                auto it = openPresents.find(surfaceId);
                if (it == openPresents.end() || it->second == std::this_thread::get_id())
                    return waited;

                waited = true;
                if (cv.wait_until(lock, deadline) == std::cv_status::timeout)
                {
                    // a present this long means the app is wedged elsewhere
                    Logger::warn("Wayland: present still in flight after the wait budget, letting a commit through");
                    return waited;
                }
            }
        }
    } // namespace

    void beginPresent(uint32_t surfaceId)
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex);
        openPresents[surfaceId] = std::this_thread::get_id();
        anyOpen.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
    }

    void endPresent(uint32_t surfaceId)
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex);
        auto it = openPresents.find(surfaceId);
        if (it == openPresents.end() || it->second != std::this_thread::get_id())
            return;

        openPresents.erase(it);
        if (openPresents.empty())
            anyOpen.store(false, std::memory_order_release);
        cv.notify_all();
    }

    bool anyPresentOpen()
    {
        return anyOpen.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
    }

    void beginCommit(uint32_t surfaceId)
    {
        if (!anyOpen.load(std::memory_order_acquire))
            return;

        std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(mutex);
        auto it = openPresents.find(surfaceId);
        if (it == openPresents.end() || it->second == std::this_thread::get_id())
            return;

        if (waitForCloseLocked(lock, surfaceId))
        {
            held.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
            Logger::info("Wayland: held a window commit behind an in-flight present");
        }
    }

    uint64_t heldCount()
    {
        return held.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }

    void setWaitBudgetForTests(uint64_t microseconds)
    {
        budgetMicros.store(microseconds, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }

    void resetForTests()
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex);
        openPresents.clear();
        anyOpen.store(false, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        held.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        budgetMicros.store(100'000, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }
} // namespace VkHook::WaylandSyncobjGate

```

`src/input/wayland_syncobj_gate.hh`:

```hh
#pragma once

#include <cstdint>

namespace VkHook
{
    // Keeps a foreign window commit out of an in-flight present. Mesa's WSI
    // sets linux-drm-syncobj points inside its present call, and a commit from
    // another thread landing between a point and the attach is a protocol
    // error hyprland answers by killing the connection. Mesa does not route
    // through any marshalling we can see, so the presenter's side is bracketed
    // around the driver present call instead, and window commits are held for
    // its duration.
    namespace WaylandSyncobjGate
    {
        // surface id of the captured wayland window, 0 when not on wayland
        uint32_t waylandSurfaceId();

        // bracket around the driver's present call
        void beginPresent(uint32_t surfaceId);
        void endPresent(uint32_t surfaceId);

        // true while any present bracket is open; lets the marshal wrapper
        // skip all work outside presents
        bool anyPresentOpen();

        // before marshalling wl_surface.commit: waits out another thread's
        // present on this surface, bounded by a budget so a wedged presenter
        // cannot park the ui thread forever
        void beginCommit(uint32_t surfaceId);

        // diagnostics: commits that were actually made to wait
        uint64_t heldCount();

        // test hooks
        void setWaitBudgetForTests(uint64_t microseconds);
        void resetForTests();
    }
} // namespace VkHook

```

`src/input/x11_display.cc`:

```cc
#include "x11_display.hh"

#include "mouse_input.hh"
#include "logger.hh"
#include "wayland_display.hh"

#include <X11/Xlib.h>
#include <X11/extensions/XInput2.h>
#include <X11/extensions/XTest.h>

#include <algorithm>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <vector>

namespace VkHook
{
    namespace
    {
        Display* g_display = nullptr;
        bool g_tried = false;
        int g_xiOpcode = 0;
        bool g_xiReady = false;

        X11KeyCallback g_keyCallback = nullptr;
        X11ButtonCallback g_buttonCallback = nullptr;
        bool g_pointerGrabActive = false;
        bool g_keyboardGrabActive = false;
        bool g_pointerHandoff = false;
        bool g_keyboardHandoff = false;
        bool g_xtestChecked = false;
        bool g_xtestReady = false;
        Cursor g_captureCursor = None;
        double g_pointerX = 0.0;
        double g_pointerY = 0.0;
        int g_pointerWidth = 1;
        int g_pointerHeight = 1;
        bool g_buttons[3] = {};
        float g_scroll = 0.0f;
        bool g_pumping = false;

        // Keys and buttons this layer released into the game when it grabbed.
        // The synthetic releases clear the server's key/button state, so a
        // re-query at release time cannot tell what is still physically down;
        // these sets are kept current from the events the grab delivers and are
        // what gets handed back. Same idea as the Wayland interpose's held keys.
        std::vector<unsigned int> g_handedKeys;
        std::vector<unsigned int> g_handedButtons;

        void initX11()
        {
            if (g_tried)
                return;
            g_tried = true;

            const char* disVar = getenv("DISPLAY");
            if (!disVar || !*disVar)
                return;

            g_display = XOpenDisplay(disVar);
            if (!g_display)
            {
                Logger::warn("X11 input: could not open DISPLAY, keyboard/mouse/blocking disabled");
                return;
            }

            int event = 0, error = 0;
            if (!XQueryExtension(g_display, "XInputExtension", &g_xiOpcode, &event, &error))
                return;

            // XI 2.0 suppresses root-selected raw events during a core grab.
            // XI 2.1 keeps delivering them, which the independent cursor needs:
            // the core grab itself only redirects core button/key events.
            int major = 2, minor = 1;
            if (XIQueryVersion(g_display, &major, &minor) != Success
                || major < 2 || (major == 2 && minor < 1))
            {
                Logger::warn("X11 input: XI 2.1 is required for independent cursor motion");
                return;
            }

            // Core events remain authoritative for grabbed keys/buttons, while
            // raw motion continues independently of game-controlled warps.
            unsigned char mask[XIMaskLen(XI_RawMotion)] = {0};
            XISetMask(mask, XI_RawKeyPress);
            XISetMask(mask, XI_RawKeyRelease);
            XISetMask(mask, XI_RawButtonPress);
            XISetMask(mask, XI_RawButtonRelease);
            XISetMask(mask, XI_RawMotion);
            XIEventMask em = {XIAllMasterDevices, sizeof(mask), mask};
            XISelectEvents(g_display, DefaultRootWindow(g_display), &em, 1);
            XFlush(g_display);
            g_xiReady = true;
        }
    }

    _XDisplay* x11Display()
    {
        initX11();
        return g_display;
    }

    bool x11Available()
    {
        initX11();
        return g_display != nullptr;
    }

    unsigned long x11GameWindow()
    {
        return getX11Window();
    }

    void setX11KeyCallback(X11KeyCallback cb)
    {
        g_keyCallback = cb;
    }

    void setX11ButtonCallback(X11ButtonCallback cb)
    {
        g_buttonCallback = cb;
    }

    // XTest is how held input is handed across a grab transition. Without it the
    // grab still works, the game is just left holding whatever was down.
    static bool xtestReady(_XDisplay* display)
    {
        if (g_xtestChecked)
            return g_xtestReady;
        g_xtestChecked = true;

        Display* d = reinterpret_cast<Display*>(display);
        int event = 0, error = 0, major = 0, minor = 0;
        g_xtestReady = d != nullptr && XTestQueryExtension(d, &event, &error, &major, &minor);
        if (!g_xtestReady)
            Logger::warn("X11 input: XTest extension missing; keys held across a grab stay stuck in the game");
        return g_xtestReady;
    }

    // Synthetic releases (toGame = false) for every key the server reports as
    // physically down, so the game's key state matches the keyboard before the
    // grab takes the events away; synthetic presses (toGame = true) for the keys
    // this layer released and has seen no real release for, so a held movement
    // key keeps working. XTest events travel the normal input path, so the game
    // sees them as its own. Must not run while our own keyboard grab is up: they
    // would be redirected into the layer instead of the game.
    static void handOffHeldKeys(bool toGame)
    {
        if (!g_display)
            return;

        if (toGame)
        {
            if (g_handedKeys.empty())
                return;
            for (unsigned int keycode : g_handedKeys)
                XTestFakeKeyEvent(g_display, keycode, True, 0);
            XSync(g_display, False);
            Logger::debug("X11 input: re-pressed " + std::to_string(g_handedKeys.size())
                          + " held key(s) after the keyboard grab");
            g_handedKeys.clear();
            return;
        }

        g_handedKeys.clear();
        if (!xtestReady(g_display))
            return;

        char keys[32] = {0};
        XQueryKeymap(g_display, keys);
        for (int keycode = 8; keycode < 256; ++keycode)
        {
            if (!(keys[keycode / 8] & (1 << (keycode % 8))))
                continue;
            XTestFakeKeyEvent(g_display, (unsigned int)keycode, False, 0);
            g_handedKeys.push_back((unsigned int)keycode);
        }
        XSync(g_display, False);

        if (!g_handedKeys.empty())
            Logger::debug("X11 input: released " + std::to_string(g_handedKeys.size())
                          + " held key(s) before the keyboard grab");
    }

    // Same contract as handOffHeldKeys, for the buttons the pointer grab takes
    // away. Core button state only covers 1-5; anything else is not holdable.
    static void handOffHeldButtons(bool toGame)
    {
        if (g_display == nullptr)
            return;

        if (toGame)
        {
            if (g_handedButtons.empty())
                return;
            for (unsigned int button : g_handedButtons)
                XTestFakeButtonEvent(g_display, button, True, 0);
            XSync(g_display, False);
            Logger::debug("X11 input: re-pressed " + std::to_string(g_handedButtons.size())
                          + " held button(s) after the pointer grab");
            g_handedButtons.clear();
            return;
        }

        g_handedButtons.clear();
        if (!xtestReady(g_display))
            return;

        Window rootRet = 0, childRet = 0;
        int rootX = 0, rootY = 0, winX = 0, winY = 0;
        unsigned int mask = 0;
        if (!XQueryPointer(g_display, DefaultRootWindow(g_display), &rootRet, &childRet,
                           &rootX, &rootY, &winX, &winY, &mask))
            return;

        for (unsigned int button = 1; button <= 5; ++button)
        {
            if (!(mask & (Button1Mask << (button - 1))))
                continue;
            XTestFakeButtonEvent(g_display, button, False, 0);
            g_handedButtons.push_back(button);
        }
        XSync(g_display, False);

        if (!g_handedButtons.empty())
            Logger::debug("X11 input: released " + std::to_string(g_handedButtons.size())
                          + " held button(s) before the pointer grab");
    }

    // Keeps the handed-over sets honest while a grab is up: the grab is where
    // press and release events for those keys and buttons arrive, so this is the
    // only place that can tell whether the player let go in the meantime.
    static void trackGrabbedInput(uint32_t keycode, uint32_t button, bool key, bool pressed)
    {
        std::vector<unsigned int>& set = key ? g_handedKeys : g_handedButtons;
        const unsigned int code = key ? keycode : button;
        auto it = std::find(set.begin(), set.end(), code);

        // Only restore input that was held BEFORE capture. A click/key begun in
        // the menu must never become a synthetic press in the game on closing.
        if (!pressed && it != set.end())
        {
            set.erase(it);
        }
    }


    static bool gameFocused(Window gameWindow)
    {
        Window focus = None;
        int revert = 0;
        XGetInputFocus(g_display, &focus, &revert);
        if (focus == PointerRoot)
        {
            Window root, child;
            int rx, ry, wx, wy;
            unsigned int mask;
            if (!XQueryPointer(g_display, DefaultRootWindow(g_display), &root, &child,
                               &rx, &ry, &wx, &wy, &mask))
                return false;
            focus = child;
        }
        const Window focusWindow = focus;
        while (focus != None && focus != DefaultRootWindow(g_display))
        {
            if (focus == gameWindow)
                return true;
            Window root, parent, *children = nullptr;
            unsigned int count = 0;
            if (!XQueryTree(g_display, focus, &root, &parent, &children, &count))
                break;
            if (children)
                XFree(children);
            focus = parent;
        }
        // A Vulkan surface may be a child of Wine's focused top-level window.
        // Accept that ancestor too, but never a root/PointerRoot desktop focus.
        if (focusWindow != None && focusWindow != DefaultRootWindow(g_display))
        {
            while (gameWindow != None && gameWindow != DefaultRootWindow(g_display))
            {
                if (gameWindow == focusWindow)
                    return true;
                Window root, parent, *children = nullptr;
                unsigned int count = 0;
                if (!XQueryTree(g_display, gameWindow, &root, &parent, &children, &count))
                    break;
                if (children)
                    XFree(children);
                gameWindow = parent;
            }
        }
        return false;
    }

    static void initializeCapturedPointer(Window window)
    {
        XWindowAttributes attr{};
        if (XGetWindowAttributes(g_display, window, &attr))
        {
            g_pointerWidth = std::max(attr.width, 1);
            g_pointerHeight = std::max(attr.height, 1);
        }
        g_pointerX = g_pointerWidth / 2.0;
        g_pointerY = g_pointerHeight / 2.0;
        for (bool& button : g_buttons)
            button = false;
        g_scroll = 0.0f;
        if (g_captureCursor == None)
        {
            const char empty = 0;
            Pixmap bitmap = XCreateBitmapFromData(g_display, window, &empty, 1, 1);
            XColor color{};
            g_captureCursor = XCreatePixmapCursor(g_display, bitmap, bitmap, &color, &color, 0, 0);
            XFreePixmap(g_display, bitmap);
        }
    }

    // The one place grabs change. Both grabs are server-side and on this
    // connection, so the game stops seeing the events entirely; the held-input
    // handoff around the first engage and the last release is what keeps the
    // game's state honest.
    void x11SetGrabStates(bool wantPointer, bool wantKeyboard)
    {
        // Open the connection here rather than requiring a poll first: a grab
        // request must not silently do nothing just because no frame has run.
        if (x11Display() == nullptr)
            return;
        const Window gameWindow = (Window)x11GameWindow();
        const bool focused = gameWindow != None && gameFocused(gameWindow);
        if (!focused)
        {
            wantPointer = false;
            wantKeyboard = false;
            // Never inject held input into a newly focused application.
            g_handedKeys.clear();
            g_handedButtons.clear();
        }
        if (wantPointer == g_pointerGrabActive && wantKeyboard == g_keyboardGrabActive
            && (wantPointer || !g_pointerHandoff) && (wantKeyboard || !g_keyboardHandoff))
            return;

        // Drain the old source before changing ownership, so raw/core copies
        // pending on either side of the grab cannot count a wheel tick twice.
        if (!g_pumping)
            pumpX11Input();
        const Window grabWindow = gameWindow;

        // Wine processes NotifyGrab asynchronously. Acquire the keyboard first
        // and retain that ownership while retrying an AlreadyGrabbed pointer.
        if (wantKeyboard && !g_keyboardGrabActive)
        {
            if (!g_keyboardHandoff)
            {
                handOffHeldKeys(false);
                g_keyboardHandoff = true;
            }
            const int status = XGrabKeyboard(g_display, grabWindow, False,
                                             GrabModeAsync, GrabModeAsync, CurrentTime);
            g_keyboardGrabActive = status == GrabSuccess;
            if (g_keyboardGrabActive && g_pointerGrabActive)
            {
                initializeCapturedPointer(grabWindow);
                XChangeActivePointerGrab(g_display, ButtonPressMask | ButtonReleaseMask | PointerMotionMask,
                                         g_captureCursor, CurrentTime);
            }
            if (status != GrabSuccess && status != AlreadyGrabbed)
                Logger::warn("X11 input: keyboard grab failed (" + std::to_string(status) + ")");
        }

        if (wantPointer != g_pointerGrabActive || (!wantPointer && g_pointerHandoff))
        {
            if (wantPointer)
            {
                // Release only once across retries while Wine processes focus.
                if (!g_pointerHandoff)
                {
                    handOffHeldButtons(false);
                    g_pointerHandoff = true;
                }
                initializeCapturedPointer(grabWindow);
                const int status = XGrabPointer(g_display, grabWindow, False,
                                                ButtonPressMask | ButtonReleaseMask | PointerMotionMask,
                                                GrabModeAsync, GrabModeAsync,
                                                g_keyboardGrabActive ? grabWindow : None,
                                                g_keyboardGrabActive ? g_captureCursor : None, CurrentTime);
                g_pointerGrabActive = status == GrabSuccess;
                if (status != GrabSuccess && status != AlreadyGrabbed)
                    Logger::warn("X11 input: pointer grab failed (" + std::to_string(status) + ")");
            }
            else
            {
                XUngrabPointer(g_display, CurrentTime);
                // now that button events reach the game again, hand back what we
                // took: the releases cleared the server's button state, so only
                // what we tracked can be re-pressed
                handOffHeldButtons(true);
                g_pointerHandoff = false;
                g_pointerGrabActive = false;
                for (bool& button : g_buttons)
                    button = false;
                g_scroll = 0.0f;
            }
        }

        // Release the pointer before allowing Wine to reacquire its capture.
        if (!wantKeyboard && (g_keyboardGrabActive || g_keyboardHandoff))
        {
            XUngrabKeyboard(g_display, CurrentTime);
            handOffHeldKeys(true);
            g_keyboardHandoff = false;
            g_keyboardGrabActive = false;
            if (g_pointerGrabActive)
                XChangeActivePointerGrab(g_display, ButtonPressMask | ButtonReleaseMask | PointerMotionMask,
                                         None, CurrentTime);
        }

        XFlush(g_display);

        Logger::debug(std::string("X11 input: grabs pointer=") + (g_pointerGrabActive ? "on" : "off")
                      + " keyboard=" + (g_keyboardGrabActive ? "on" : "off"));
    }


    bool x11GrabActive()
    {
        return g_pointerGrabActive || g_keyboardGrabActive;
    }

    bool x11PointerGrabActive()
    {
        return g_pointerGrabActive;
    }

    bool x11GameFocused()
    {
        return x11Available() && gameFocused((Window)x11GameWindow());
    }

    bool x11CapturedMouseState(MouseState& state)
    {
        if (!g_pointerGrabActive || !g_keyboardGrabActive)
            return false;
        state.x = static_cast<int>(g_pointerX);
        state.y = static_cast<int>(g_pointerY);
        state.leftButton = g_buttons[0];
        state.middleButton = g_buttons[1];
        state.rightButton = g_buttons[2];
        state.scrollDelta = g_scroll;
        g_scroll = 0.0f;
        return true;
    }

    void pumpX11Input()
    {
        if (!x11Available())
            return;
        g_pumping = true;
        if ((g_pointerGrabActive || g_keyboardGrabActive) && !gameFocused((Window)x11GameWindow()))
            x11SetGrabStates(false, false);

        while (XPending(g_display) > 0)
        {
            XEvent ev;
            XNextEvent(g_display, &ev);

            if (ev.type == GenericEvent && ev.xcookie.extension == g_xiOpcode
                && XGetEventData(g_display, &ev.xcookie))
            {
                switch (ev.xcookie.evtype)
                {
                case XI_RawMotion:
                    if (g_pointerGrabActive && g_keyboardGrabActive)
                    {
                        const auto* motion = static_cast<XIRawEvent*>(ev.xcookie.data);
                        const double* value = motion->raw_values;
                        for (int axis = 0; axis < motion->valuators.mask_len * 8; ++axis)
                        {
                            if (!XIMaskIsSet(motion->valuators.mask, axis))
                                continue;
                            if (axis == 0)
                                g_pointerX = std::clamp(g_pointerX + *value, 0.0, double(g_pointerWidth - 1));
                            else if (axis == 1)
                                g_pointerY = std::clamp(g_pointerY + *value, 0.0, double(g_pointerHeight - 1));
                            ++value;
                        }
                    }
                    break;
                case XI_RawKeyPress:
                case XI_RawKeyRelease:
                    // the keyboard grab makes core events authoritative; raw
                    // here would double every press on servers that still
                    // deliver it
                    if (!g_keyboardGrabActive && g_keyCallback)
                    {
                        const bool pressed = ev.xcookie.evtype == XI_RawKeyPress;
                        g_keyCallback(((XIRawEvent*)ev.xcookie.data)->detail, pressed);
                    }
                    break;
                case XI_RawButtonPress:
                case XI_RawButtonRelease:
                    if (!g_pointerGrabActive && g_buttonCallback)
                    {
                        const bool pressed = ev.xcookie.evtype == XI_RawButtonPress;
                        g_buttonCallback(((XIRawEvent*)ev.xcookie.data)->detail, pressed);
                    }
                    break;
                default:
                    break;
                }
                XFreeEventData(g_display, &ev.xcookie);
            }
            else if (ev.type == KeyPress || ev.type == KeyRelease)
            {
                // consumed while grabbed (raw events can stop during a core
                // grab) or as the no-XInput2 fallback; outside both, raw
                // already delivered this key and core would double it.
                if ((g_keyboardGrabActive || !g_xiReady) && g_keyCallback)
                    g_keyCallback(ev.xkey.keycode, ev.type == KeyPress);
                if (g_keyboardGrabActive)
                    trackGrabbedInput(ev.xkey.keycode, 0, true, ev.type == KeyPress);
            }
            else if (ev.type == ButtonPress || ev.type == ButtonRelease)
            {
                if ((g_pointerGrabActive || !g_xiReady) && g_buttonCallback)
                    g_buttonCallback(ev.xbutton.button, ev.type == ButtonPress);
                if (g_pointerGrabActive)
                {
                    const unsigned int button = ev.xbutton.button;
                    const bool pressed = ev.type == ButtonPress;
                    if (button >= 1 && button <= 3)
                        g_buttons[button - 1] = pressed;
                    else if (pressed && (button == 4 || button == 5))
                        g_scroll += button == 4 ? 1.0f : -1.0f;
                    trackGrabbedInput(0, button, false, pressed);
                }
            }
        }
        g_pumping = false;
    }
} // namespace VkHook

```

`src/input/x11_display.hh`:

```hh
#pragma once

#include <cstdint>

struct _XDisplay;

namespace VkHook
{
    struct MouseState;
    // Shared X11 connection for the input backends and the input blocker. One
    // connection means one event queue: XInput2 raw events, active-grab events,
    // and query-based polling all drain from the same place.
    _XDisplay* x11Display();
    bool x11Available();

    // The game window captured from the Vulkan surface, as an XID, or 0.
    unsigned long x11GameWindow();

    // Raw key transitions, from XInput2 and from an active grab.
    using X11KeyCallback = void (*)(uint32_t keycode, bool pressed);
    using X11ButtonCallback = void (*)(uint32_t button, bool pressed);
    void setX11KeyCallback(X11KeyCallback cb);
    void setX11ButtonCallback(X11ButtonCallback cb);

    // Drains pending events and hands key/button transitions to the callbacks.
    // Call once per frame; a no-op when X11 is absent.
    void pumpX11Input();

    // Holds or releases a server-side grab on the game window so the game stops
    // seeing input while the overlay is used. Call pumpX11Input() on every frame
    // to keep the redirected events flowing.
    //
    // The pointer grab blocks clicks and motion, the keyboard grab blocks keys.
    // The keyboard is acquired first for an interactive menu: Wine reacts to
    // NotifyGrab by releasing the game's capture. Failed grabs remain inactive
    // and may be retried on the next frame.
    void x11SetGrabStates(bool pointer, bool keyboard);
    bool x11GrabActive();
    bool x11PointerGrabActive();
    bool x11GameFocused();
    // Supplies the virtual pointer and event-driven buttons while captured.
    // Raw device deltas, not game-controlled absolute pointer warps, move it.
    bool x11CapturedMouseState(MouseState& state);
} // namespace VkHook
```
