`src/tests/smoke_vkcube.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# smoke test: run vkcube under the freshly built layer and fail if it dies
#
# the point is not that vkcube renders correctly, it is that driving a real
# swapchain through the layer for a few seconds does not take the process down.
# that catches the class of bug unit tests cannot: a bad interceptor, a null
# handle dereference, a use-after-free on a handle whose lifetime we guessed at.
#
# usage: src/tests/smoke_vkcube.sh [LIBVKHOOK_SO] [SECONDS]
#
# VKHOOK_SMOKE_DEPTH_REFRESH sets how often, in ms, the run forces a depth
# re-detect (default 500), which is what drives the rebuild assertions below.
# VKHOOK_SMOKE_REBUILD_MODE=1 seeds the fast rebuild path instead of the safe
# default; on a GPU, run both to cover the two.
#
# needs a display. on CI wrap it: xvfb-run -a src/tests/smoke_vkcube.sh
# there is no GPU on a CI runner either, so point VK_ICD_FILENAMES at lavapipe
# or the loader will find nothing to run on.

set -euo pipefail

# resolved from the script's own location rather than the cwd, so the shader
# fixtures are found when this is invoked from anywhere -- CI in particular runs
# it through xvfb-run from the repository root, and a cwd-relative path would
# quietly seed no effect at all, turning the run into a pass-through test that
# looks like it passed.
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

LIBRARY="${1:-build/src/libvkhook.so}"
DURATION="${2:-11}"
LAYER_NAME="VK_LAYER_VKHOOK_smoke_test"
# the installed production layer, which on a developer machine would otherwise
# be discovered alongside ours and could shadow the build we actually want to test
INSTALLED_LAYER="VK_LAYER_VKHOOK_post_processing"

if [[ -t 1 ]]; then
    B='\033[1m'; BLUE='\033[34m'; GREEN='\033[32m'; YELLOW='\033[33m'; RED='\033[31m'; DIM='\033[2m'; NC='\033[0m'
else
    B=''; BLUE=''; GREEN=''; YELLOW=''; RED=''; DIM=''; NC=''
fi

say() { printf "${BLUE}  →${NC} %s\n" "$*"; }
ok() { printf "${GREEN}  ✓${NC} %s\n" "$*"; }
warn() { printf "${YELLOW}  !${NC} %s\n" "$*"; }
die() {
    printf "${RED}  ✗${NC} %s\n" "$*" >&2
    if [[ -n "${WORK_DIR:-}" && -d "$WORK_DIR" ]]; then
        printf "  ${DIM}artifacts kept: %s${NC}\n" "$WORK_DIR" >&2
    fi
    exit 1
}
finish() { printf "\n${BLUE}${B}%s${NC}\n" "$*"; }

command -v vkcube >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "vkcube not found; install vulkan-tools"
[[ -f "$LIBRARY" ]] || die "layer library not found: $LIBRARY (build it first)"
LIBRARY="$(cd "$(dirname "$LIBRARY")" && pwd)/$(basename "$LIBRARY")"

if [[ -z "${DISPLAY:-}" && -z "${WAYLAND_DISPLAY:-}" ]]; then
    # A headless runner has no display at all and vkcube cannot open a window
    # without one. Re-exec under xvfb-run so the same command works on a
    # developer desktop and on CI. The env marker keeps a broken xvfb-run from
    # turning this into an exec loop.
    if [[ -z "${VKHOOK_SMOKE_XVFB:-}" ]] && command -v xvfb-run >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        VKHOOK_SMOKE_XVFB=1 exec xvfb-run -a "$0" "$@"
    fi
    die "no display, and xvfb-run is not available to provide one"
fi

WORK_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
cleanup() {
    local status=$?
    trap - EXIT
    if (( status == 0 )) && [[ -n "${WORK_DIR:-}" && -d "$WORK_DIR" ]]; then
        rm -rf -- "$WORK_DIR"
    fi
    exit "$status"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

# A manifest of our own, under a layer name nothing else uses, so the loader
# cannot mistake it for an installed copy and drop it as a duplicate.
LAYER_DIR="$WORK_DIR/layer"
CONFIG_DIR="$WORK_DIR/config"
mkdir -p "$LAYER_DIR" "$CONFIG_DIR"
cat >"$LAYER_DIR/$LAYER_NAME.json" <<JSON
{
  "file_format_version": "1.0.0",
  "layer": {
    "name": "$LAYER_NAME",
    "type": "GLOBAL",
    "library_path": "$LIBRARY",
    "api_version": "1.3.223",
    "implementation_version": "1",
    "description": "vkhook smoke test",
    "functions": {
      "vkGetInstanceProcAddr": "VkHook_GetInstanceProcAddr",
      "vkGetDeviceProcAddr": "VkHook_GetDeviceProcAddr"
    },
    "enable_environment": { "ENABLE_VKHOOK": "1" },
    "disable_environment": { "DISABLE_VKHOOK": "1" }
  }
}
JSON
jq -e . "$LAYER_DIR/$LAYER_NAME.json" >/dev/null || die "generated manifest is not valid json"

# Seed a config that actually exercises the layer. With no config the layer
# starts with no effects enabled and takes the pass-through path, which is close
# to doing nothing at all, so a crash-only smoke test would be asserting almost
# nothing. Enabling one depth-consuming effect forces the capture and resolve
# machinery to run, which is where the layer actually earns its crash reports.
#
# The depth settings are pinned rather than left to defaults so the test is not
# quietly at the mercy of whatever a previous run happened to write:
#   depthSourceChannel = 0 -> Luminance/Red, the standard Vulkan depth layout
#   depthInvert        = false -> near/far not flipped
seed_config() {
    local base="$CONFIG_DIR/VkHook"
    mkdir -p "$base/configs/shaders" "$base/reshade/packages/Shaders"

    cat >"$base/VkHook.conf" <<'CONF'
enableOnLaunch = true
overlayKey = Home
reloadKey = F10
maxEffects = 10
autoApply = true
autoApplyDelay = 200
depthCapture = on
showDebugWindow = false
depthResolveMode = 0
depthManualPin =
depthTransientWorkaround = true
depthCaptureMethod = 1
depthSourceChannel = 0
depthInvert = false
CONF

    # The effect is a real, community-maintained ReShade shader rather than
    # something written for this test. That matters: a hand-written effect proved
    # the depth path ran, but exercised almost none of the compile pipeline. This
    # one carries uniform preprocessor definitions, a localisation include and a
    # large UI parameter set, so it goes through the same machinery a user's shader
    # does. The files live in src/tests/fixtures -- see the README there for
    # provenance and the open licence question on two of the three.
    local fixtures="$SCRIPT_DIR/fixtures"
    for fixture in DisplayDepth.fx ReShade.fxh DisplayDepth_L10N.fxh; do
        [[ -f "$fixtures/$fixture" ]] || die "missing test fixture: $fixtures/$fixture"
        cp "$fixtures/$fixture" "$base/reshade/packages/Shaders/$fixture"
    done

    # vkcube is the game name the layer derives from the process, so the config
    # and profile files are keyed on it. Parameters are deliberately omitted so the
    # effect runs on the defaults declared in the shader itself.
    cat >"$base/configs/vkcube.conf" <<'CONF'
DisplayDepth = DisplayDepth.fx
effects = DisplayDepth
CONF

    cat >"$base/configs/shaders/vkcube@smoke.ini" <<'INI'
Techniques=DisplayDepth@DisplayDepth.fx
TechniqueSorting=DisplayDepth@DisplayDepth.fx

[DisplayDepth.fx]
INI

    printf 'smoke\n' >"$base/configs/shaders/vkcube.last-profile"

    # Exercise automatic or manual scale without changing the user's config.
    if [[ -n "${VKHOOK_SMOKE_UI_SCALE:-}" ]]; then
        printf 'uiScale = %s\n' "$VKHOOK_SMOKE_UI_SCALE" >>"$base/VkHook.conf"
    fi

    # Which path the forced rebuilds below take: 0 = safe (idles the queue),
    # 1 = fast (fence-gated). Unset leaves the shipped default (safe).
    if [[ -n "${VKHOOK_SMOKE_REBUILD_MODE:-}" ]]; then
        printf 'depthRebuildMode = %s\n' "$VKHOOK_SMOKE_REBUILD_MODE" >>"$base/VkHook.conf"
    fi
}

seed_config

say "layer      $LIBRARY"
say "duration   ${DURATION}s"

# VK_LOADER_LAYERS_ENABLE is what guarantees our layer is the one that ends up in
# the chain. Without it, a VkHook already installed on the machine wins and the
# run silently tests the installed build instead of this one.
#
# The XDG_CONFIG_HOME redirect sends the layer's own log somewhere disposable, so
# "did the layer actually engage" is answerable without reading a stale log from
# an earlier run, and a local run cannot scribble on a real config.
set +e
# Debug level is set here rather than left to the ambient default, because the
# assertions below need lines that only exist at debug. Notably "detected depth
# image", which is the only way to tell "the app gave us no depth at all" (a
# real failure) apart from "depth was found but resolve never engaged" (an
# environment limitation). At the default info level those two look identical,
# so the test cannot fail correctly without asking for debug.
VK_LOADER_DEBUG=layer \
    VKHOOK_LOG_LEVEL=debug \
    VKHOOK_SMOKE_DEPTH_REFRESH="${VKHOOK_SMOKE_DEPTH_REFRESH:-500}" \
    VK_LOADER_LAYERS_ENABLE="$LAYER_NAME" \
    VK_LOADER_LAYERS_DISABLE="$INSTALLED_LAYER" \
    VK_LAYER_PATH="$LAYER_DIR" \
    ENABLE_VKHOOK=1 \
    XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$CONFIG_DIR" \
    timeout "$DURATION" vkcube >"$WORK_DIR/vkcube.log" 2>&1
STATUS=$?
set -e

LOADED=no
if grep -qF "$LIBRARY" "$WORK_DIR/vkcube.log"; then
    LOADED=yes
fi

if [[ "$LOADED" != yes ]]; then
    printf "%s\n" "--- vkcube + loader output ---" >&2
    cat "$WORK_DIR/vkcube.log" >&2
    die "the loader never loaded $LIBRARY, so this run proves nothing. an installed copy of the layer may be shadowing it; check the loader lines above."
fi
ok "layer loaded from the build directory"

LAYER_LOG="$CONFIG_DIR/VkHook/vkhook.log"
if [[ -s "$LAYER_LOG" ]]; then
    ok "layer engaged ($(wc -l <"$LAYER_LOG") log lines)"
else
    die "layer loaded but wrote no log; it may not have reached initialisation"
fi

# A panic means the layer hit a state it does not trust and soft-disabled itself
# or tore the device down; for a smoke run that is a failure even when the
# process limps on to the end, because nothing after it proves anything.
if grep -qF 'VkHook panic' "$LAYER_LOG"; then
    grep -F 'VkHook panic' "$LAYER_LOG" >&2
    die "the layer panicked during the run (see the line above)"
fi

# Assert the effect actually engaged, not merely that the layer loaded.
#
# Without this the test degrades silently. Every reason the seed can fail -- a
# fixture not copied, a shader that stops compiling, an effect name that no
# longer resolves -- results in the layer running with nothing enabled, taking
# the pass-through path and surviving. The run still reports PASSED, having
# asserted almost nothing.
#
# The signal is [effect-built], logged at the end of the effect's constructor.
# That makes it a creation-time fact: reaching the line means the shader was
# found, parsed, compiled and turned into render passes. An earlier version of
# this assertion matched the destructor's trace instead, which was wrong -- a
# trace from a destructor only appears if something tears the effect down, and
# on a CI runner the normal ending is vkcube being killed by the timeout, so it
# never got the chance. That assertion passed locally only because the resize
# reload happened to destroy effects mid-run, and failed on CI for the same
# reason inverted.
#
# passes= must be non-zero: zero would mean the effect object exists but never
# got a pipeline, so it never drew.
if grep -qE '\[effect-built\] DisplayDepth passes=[1-9]' "$LAYER_LOG"; then
    ok "DisplayDepth compiled and built a render pass"
elif grep -q 'pass through only' "$LAYER_LOG"; then
    # The layer supports Wayland surfaces only. On X11 it deliberately does
    # nothing at all, so there is no effect to build and nothing to assert about
    # the effect pipeline here. This is the CI configuration, which is why the
    # run is a pass-through check on CI and a real one locally.
    warn "non-Wayland surface: layer is pass-through, effect pipeline not exercised (CI runs this way)"
else
    printf '%s\n' "--- layer log ---" >&2
    cat "$LAYER_LOG" >&2
    die "DisplayDepth was never built, so this run exercised the pass-through path and proves nothing about the effect pipeline. The log above shows how far it got."
fi

# Depth resolve is reported, not asserted, and that is deliberate.
#
# Under X11 plus lavapipe -- which is exactly what CI runs -- the layer finds
# vkcube's depth attachment ("detected depth image") but never builds the
# resolve resources for it, so hasDepth is false for every frame and nothing
# logs the resolve. Confirmed pre-existing: the last green commit behaves
# identically. The earlier version of this test asserted on it and turned CI
# red on six consecutive commits, which says nothing about the code.
#
# The cost is real and worth stating: on a software-Vulkan runner this test
# cannot tell you the depth path works. It can only tell you the layer loaded,
# built a real effect from a real community shader, and did not crash. The
# depth path needs a GPU to be covered, and nothing in this script can conjure
# one.
if grep -q 'depth resolve source view changed' "$LAYER_LOG"; then
    ok "depth resolve engaged"

    # VKHOOK_SMOKE_DEPTH_REFRESH drops the depth selection every 500ms, the
    # same as clicking "Refresh depth buffers", so the rebuild below runs
    # repeatedly while the queue is loaded. A rebuild frees command buffers and
    # tears down resolve targets: getting the fence gating or the safe-mode wait
    # wrong turns that into a GPU hang, which reads here as a missing rebuild
    # (present stopped) or a device-lost panic, not as a silent difference.
    rebuilds=$(grep -c 'deferred depth change rebuilt presented swapchain' "$LAYER_LOG" || true)
    (( rebuilds > 0 )) || die "the refresh hook ran but no depth rebuild happened; the rebuild path is not covered"
    ok "$rebuilds depth rebuild(s) while presenting"
elif grep -q 'detected depth image' "$LAYER_LOG"; then
    warn "depth attachment seen but resolve never engaged (pre-existing under X11 + lavapipe; CI cannot cover the depth path)"
else
    die "no depth attachment detected at all. DisplayDepth uses depth, so capture is off or the app never provided one; the run survived but exercised nothing depth-related."
fi

# 124 is what timeout reports when it had to stop the process, which is the only
# outcome that means "still alive when we stopped watching".
case "$STATUS" in
    124) ok "vkcube survived ${DURATION}s without crashing" ;;
    0)   ok "vkcube exited cleanly on its own" ;;
    137) die "vkcube was SIGKILLed (exit 137), usually the OOM killer" ;;
    139) die "vkcube segfaulted (exit 139) under the layer" ;;
    134) die "vkcube aborted (exit 134) under the layer" ;;
    *)
        printf "%s\n" "--- vkcube output ---" >&2
        cat "$WORK_DIR/vkcube.log" >&2
        die "vkcube exited with $STATUS"
        ;;
esac

finish "smoke test PASSED"

```

`src/tests/test_depth_clear_smoke.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Opt-in Xlib/GPU regression for an in-scope D24S8 depth clear.

From the repository root, after building the corresponding layer/shader headers:

  g++ -std=c++17 -O2 -Ibuild-gcc/src/libvkhook.so.p \
    src/tests/depth_clear_smoke.cc -o build-gcc/depth-clear-smoke -lvulkan -lX11
  zig c++ \
    -target x86-linux-gnu.2.34 -std=c++17 -O2 -idirafter /usr/include \
    -Ibuild-zig32/src/libvkhook.so.p src/tests/depth_clear_smoke.cc \
    -L/usr/lib32 -lvulkan -lX11 -Wl,--allow-shlib-undefined -o build-zig32/depth-clear-smoke

  python3 \
    src/tests/test_depth_clear_smoke.py --binary "$PWD/build-gcc/depth-clear-smoke" \
    --layer "$PWD/build-gcc/src/libvkhook.so" --artifacts "$PWD/build-gcc"
  python3 \
    src/tests/test_depth_clear_smoke.py --binary "$PWD/build-zig32/depth-clear-smoke" \
    --layer "$PWD/build-zig32/src/libvkhook.so" --artifacts "$PWD/build-zig32"

Pass --layer /absolute/baseline.so for the unfixed-layer negative control.
Keep the test's own window visible/unobscured. --width 3840 --height 2160
reproduces the dump's dimensions when the display can show the entire window.
By default, exercise dynamic rendering with GENERAL depth; --legacy tests render passes.
No global input injection, desktop capture, or user configuration writes.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import re
import resource
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

from test_shared_texture_smoke import X11


EFFECT = """
texture SceneColor : COLOR;
sampler SceneColorSampler { Texture = SceneColor; };
texture SceneDepth : DEPTH;
sampler SceneDepthSampler { Texture = SceneDepth; };
void DepthClearVS(uint id : SV_VertexID, out float4 position : SV_Position,
                  out float2 texcoord : TEXCOORD)
{
    texcoord = float2(id == 2 ? 2.0 : 0.0, id == 1 ? 2.0 : 0.0);
    position = float4(texcoord * float2(2.0, -2.0) + float2(-1.0, 1.0), 0.0, 1.0);
}
float4 DepthClearPS(float4 position : SV_Position, float2 uv : TEXCOORD) : SV_Target
{
    if (uv.y < 0.5) return tex2D(SceneColorSampler, uv);
    float depth = tex2D(SceneDepthSampler, uv).r;
    return float4(depth, depth, depth, 1.0);
}
technique DepthClearProbe
{
    pass { VertexShader = DepthClearVS; PixelShader = DepthClearPS; }
}
"""


def seed(work, args):
    config = work / "config" / "VkHook"
    profiles = config / "configs" / "shaders"
    shaders = config / "reshade" / "Shaders"
    layers = work / "layers"
    for directory in (profiles, shaders, layers, work / "home", work / "data", work / "cache"):
        directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    name = "VK_LAYER_VKHOOK_post_processing"
    manifest = {"file_format_version": "1.0.0", "layer": {
        "name": name, "type": "GLOBAL", "library_path": str(args.layer),
        "api_version": "1.3.223", "implementation_version": "1",
        "description": "VkHook depth clear GPU regression",
        "functions": {"vkGetInstanceProcAddr": "VkHook_GetInstanceProcAddr",
                      "vkGetDeviceProcAddr": "VkHook_GetDeviceProcAddr"}}}
    (layers / "VkHook.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest), encoding="utf-8")
    effect_name = "DepthClearProbe"
    effect = EFFECT
    (shaders / (effect_name + ".fx")).write_text(effect, encoding="utf-8")
    (config / "VkHook.conf").write_text(
        "enableOnLaunch = true\noverlayKey = Home\nreloadKey = F10\n"
        "maxEffects = 10\nautoApply = false\ndepthCapture = on\nshowDebugWindow = false\n",
        encoding="utf-8")
    game = args.binary.name
    (config / "configs" / (game + ".conf")).write_text(
        f"{effect_name} = {effect_name}.fx\neffects = {effect_name}\n", encoding="utf-8")
    (profiles / (game + "@depth-clear.ini")).write_text(
        f"Techniques={effect_name}@{effect_name}.fx\n"
        f"TechniqueSorting={effect_name}@{effect_name}.fx\n\n[{effect_name}.fx]\n", encoding="utf-8")
    (profiles / (game + ".last-profile")).write_text("depth-clear\n", encoding="utf-8")
    env = {key: value for key, value in os.environ.items()
           if not key.startswith(("VKHOOK_", "VK_LAYER_", "VK_ADD_LAYER_", "VK_LOADER_LAYERS_"))
           and key not in ("VK_INSTANCE_LAYERS", "ENABLE_VKHOOK", "DISABLE_VKHOOK")}
    authority = Path(os.environ.get("HOME", "")) / ".Xauthority"
    if "XAUTHORITY" not in env and authority.is_file():
        env["XAUTHORITY"] = str(authority.resolve())
    env.update(HOME=str(work / "home"), XDG_CONFIG_HOME=str(work / "config"),
               XDG_DATA_HOME=str(work / "data"), XDG_CACHE_HOME=str(work / "cache"),
               VK_LAYER_PATH=str(layers), VK_INSTANCE_LAYERS=name,
               VK_LOADER_LAYERS_DISABLE="~implicit", DISABLE_VKHOOK="1",
               VK_LOADER_DEBUG="layer", VKHOOK_LOG_LEVEL="debug")
    if args.validation:
        # Validation is BELOW VkHook so it observes injected commands too.
        env["VK_INSTANCE_LAYERS"] += ":VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation"
        env["VK_LAYER_PATH"] += ":/usr/share/vulkan/explicit_layer.d:/etc/vulkan/explicit_layer.d"
    return env


def evidence(text, width, height, legacy):
    layout = 3 if legacy else 1
    backend = "(?:shader|copy)" if legacy else "shader"
    required = {
        "selected D24S8 depth": rf"active depth state updated[^\n]*format=129[^\n]*extent={width}x{height}[^\n]*observedLayout={layout}(?:\s|$)",
        "single-sample snapshot": rf"depth resolve path: {backend} observedLayout={layout} samples=1(?:\s|$)",
        "offscreen render scope with real draws": r"depth candidate promoted[^\n]*draws=[1-9][0-9]* presentable=false",
    }
    found = {}
    for label, pattern in required.items():
        match = re.search(pattern, text)
        if not match:
            raise RuntimeError("missing layer evidence: " + label)
        found[label] = match.group(0).strip()
    return found


def pixels_match(samples, phase):
    if not samples:
        return False
    # X11 helper returns a 3x3 grid. Avoid the half-width/half-height edges.
    expected = {0: (0, 255, 0) if phase == "clear" else (255, 0, 0),
                2: (255, 0, 0),
                6: (191, 191, 191) if phase == "clear" else (64, 64, 64),
                8: (64, 64, 64)}
    return all(all(abs(actual - target) <= 12 for actual, target in zip(samples[index]["rgb"], color))
               for index, color in expected.items())


def run(args):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="vkhook-depth-clear-") as temporary:
        work = Path(temporary)
        child, x11 = None, None
        samples, selected = {}, {}
        result = 1
        try:
            env = seed(work, args)
            x11 = X11()
            log = work / "application.log"
            layer_log = work / "config" / "VkHook" / "vkhook.log"
            with log.open("wb") as output:
                command = [str(args.binary), "--width", str(args.width), "--height", str(args.height)]
                if args.legacy:
                    command.append("--legacy")
                child = subprocess.Popen(command,
                                         env=env, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=output, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                                         preexec_fn=lambda: resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_CORE, (0, 0)))
                phases = ("warmup", "clear")
                for phase in phases:
                    deadline = time.monotonic() + args.timeout
                    consecutive = 0
                    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
                        if child.poll() is not None:
                            raise RuntimeError("application exited during " + phase + ": " + str(child.returncode))
                        text = log.read_text(errors="replace")
                        match = re.search(r"^WINDOW=(\d+)$", text, re.MULTILINE)
                        if match and "READY phase=" + phase in text:
                            window = int(match.group(1))
                            if x11.name(window) != "VkHook depth clear regression":
                                raise RuntimeError("test window identity changed")
                            samples[phase] = x11.sample(window)
                            consecutive = consecutive + 1 if pixels_match(samples[phase], phase) else 0
                            if consecutive >= 3:
                                break
                        time.sleep(0.2)
                    else:
                        raise RuntimeError("timed out waiting for " + phase + " color AND captured depth pixels; "
                                           "keep the test window visible and unobscured")
                    if str(args.layer) not in text:
                        raise RuntimeError("loader trace does not identify requested layer")
                    if not layer_log.is_file():
                        raise RuntimeError("layer initialization log missing")
                    layer_text = layer_log.read_text(errors="replace")
                    selected[phase] = evidence(layer_text, args.width, args.height, args.legacy)
                    print(phase + " selected-source evidence: " + json.dumps(selected[phase]), flush=True)
                    print(phase + " window color/depth pixels: " + json.dumps(samples[phase]), flush=True)
                    # The risky clear cannot be recorded until shader resources
                    # are proven active by both log and actual depth texture output.
                    child.stdin.write(b"continue\n")
                    child.stdin.flush()
                child.stdin.close()
                child.wait(timeout=args.timeout)
                if child.returncode != 0:
                    raise RuntimeError("unclean shutdown: " + str(child.returncode))
            text = log.read_text(errors="replace")
            if "PASS clean_shutdown=true" not in text:
                raise RuntimeError("missing clean-shutdown marker")
            all_logs = text + "\n" + layer_log.read_text(errors="replace")
            if re.search(r"Validation Error|VUID-|UNASSIGNED-.*(?:Error|error)", all_logs):
                raise RuntimeError("Vulkan validation reported an invalid command; see artifacts")
            print("PASS: in-scope depth clear, continued draws, GPU color readback, captured depth before/after clear, clean shutdown",
                  flush=True)
            result = 0
        except (OSError, RuntimeError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired, KeyboardInterrupt) as error:
            print("FAIL: " + (str(error) or type(error).__name__), flush=True)
            result = 130 if isinstance(error, KeyboardInterrupt) else 1
        finally:
            if child is not None and child.poll() is None:
                child.terminate()
                try:
                    child.wait(timeout=5)
                except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                    child.kill()
                    child.wait()
            if child is not None and child.stdin is not None and not child.stdin.closed:
                try:
                    child.stdin.close()
                except OSError:
                    pass
            if x11 is not None:
                x11.close()
            if args.artifacts:
                args.artifacts.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                destination = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="depth-clear-", dir=args.artifacts))
                for path in work.rglob("*.log"):
                    target = destination / path.relative_to(work)
                    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                    shutil.copyfile(path, target)
                (destination / "evidence.json").write_text(json.dumps(
                    {"pixels": samples, "selected_depth": selected, "exit_code": result}, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
                print("Artifacts: " + str(destination), flush=True)
            if result:
                print("Last sampled pixels: " + json.dumps(samples), flush=True)
                for path in sorted(work.rglob("*.log")):
                    print("--- " + str(path.relative_to(work)) + " (last 64 KiB) ---", flush=True)
                    print(path.read_text(errors="replace")[-65536:], flush=True)
        return result


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("--binary", type=Path, required=True, help="explicit path to architecture-matched smoke binary")
    parser.add_argument("--layer", type=Path, required=True, help="explicit path to layer under test")
    parser.add_argument("--artifacts", type=Path, help="retain success/failure logs and pixel evidence here")
    parser.add_argument("--timeout", type=float, default=90, help="deadline per phase, in seconds")
    parser.add_argument("--width", type=int, default=640)
    parser.add_argument("--height", type=int, default=480)
    parser.add_argument("--validation", action="store_true", help="also enable installed architecture-matched Khronos validation")
    parser.add_argument("--legacy", action="store_true", help="use legacy render passes instead of dynamic rendering")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    for name in ("binary", "layer"):
        path = getattr(args, name).resolve()
        if not path.is_file():
            parser.error("--" + name + " must name an existing file")
        setattr(args, name, path)
    if not os.environ.get("DISPLAY"):
        parser.error("DISPLAY and appropriate XAUTHORITY are required")
    if not 0 < args.timeout <= 300 or not all(64 <= value <= 8192 for value in (args.width, args.height)):
        parser.error("timeout must be in (0, 300]; dimensions must be in [64, 8192]")
    return run(args)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

`src/tests/test_reshade_shaders.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Compile every ReShade .fx shader in a tree or fetched EffectPackages set."""

import argparse
import configparser
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import urllib.request
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path


DEFAULT_MANIFEST_URL = (
    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sorche942/VkHook/refs/heads/main/assets/EffectPackages.ini"
)


def fetch_manifest(url: str, destination: Path) -> None:
    request = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "VkHook-tests"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=60) as response, destination.open("wb") as output:
        shutil.copyfileobj(response, output)


def install_manifest_packages(manifest: Path, work_dir: Path, shader_dir: Path) -> None:
    config = configparser.ConfigParser(strict=False)
    config.read_string(manifest.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig"))
    shader_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    failures = []
    installed = 0
    for section in config.sections():
        package = config[section]
        name = package.get("PackageName", section)
        url = package.get("DownloadUrl")
        if not url:
            continue

        install_path = package.get("InstallPath", r".\reshade-shaders\Shaders")
        install_path = install_path.replace("\\", "/").lstrip("./")
        subdir = install_path.replace("reshade-shaders/Shaders", "", 1).strip("/")
        target_dir = shader_dir / subdir if subdir else shader_dir
        target_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        allowed = {value.strip() for value in package.get("EffectFiles", "").split(",") if value.strip()}
        denied = {value.strip() for value in package.get("DenyEffectFiles", "").split(",") if value.strip()}
        archive_path = work_dir / f"{section}.zip"
        extract_dir = work_dir / section
        try:
            request = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "VkHook-tests"})
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=120) as response, archive_path.open("wb") as output:
                shutil.copyfileobj(response, output)
            extract_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            with zipfile.ZipFile(archive_path) as archive:
                for member in archive.infolist():
                    member_path = Path(member.filename)
                    if member_path.is_absolute() or ".." in member_path.parts:
                        continue
                    if member.is_dir():
                        continue
                    filename = member_path.name
                    if filename in denied or not filename.endswith((".fx", ".fxh")):
                        continue
                    if filename.endswith(".fx") and allowed and filename not in allowed:
                        continue
                    output_path = extract_dir / filename
                    with archive.open(member) as source, output_path.open("wb") as output:
                        shutil.copyfileobj(source, output)

            copied = 0
            for source in extract_dir.iterdir():
                if source.is_file() and source.name.endswith((".fx", ".fxh")):
                    shutil.copy2(source, target_dir / source.name)
                    copied += 1
            if copied == 0:
                failures.append(f"{name}: package yielded no matching shader files")
            else:
                installed += 1
                print(f"fetched {name}: {copied} shader/include file(s)", flush=True)
        except Exception as error:  # Network and archive failures need package context.
            failures.append(f"{name}: {error}")

    if failures:
        raise RuntimeError("Package fetch failures:\n  " + "\n  ".join(failures))
    if installed == 0:
        raise RuntimeError("EffectPackages.ini did not provide any shader packages")


def compile_shaders(shader_check: Path, shader_dir: Path) -> int:
    shaders = sorted(shader_dir.rglob("*.fx"))
    if not shaders:
        print(f"No .fx shaders found under {shader_dir}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    include_dirs = sorted({shader_dir, *(path.parent for path in shader_dir.rglob("*.fxh"))})
    command_prefix = [str(shader_check)]
    for include_dir in include_dirs:
        command_prefix.extend(["--include", str(include_dir)])

    failures = []
    print(f"compiling {len(shaders)} ReShade shader(s) from {shader_dir}", flush=True)
    for index, shader in enumerate(shaders, start=1):
        result = subprocess.run(
            [*command_prefix, str(shader)],
            check=False,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
        )
        if result.returncode != 0:
            details = (result.stdout + result.stderr).strip()
            failures.append((shader, details))
            print(f"failed [{index}/{len(shaders)}]: {shader}", flush=True)
        elif index % 25 == 0 or index == len(shaders):
            print(f"compiled [{index}/{len(shaders)}]", flush=True)

    if failures:
        print(f"\n{len(failures)} of {len(shaders)} shader(s) failed:", file=sys.stderr)
        for shader, details in failures:
            print(f"\n--- {shader} ---\n{details}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    print(f"all {len(shaders)} ReShade shader(s) compiled successfully", flush=True)
    return 0


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--shader-check", required=True, type=Path, help="vkhook-shader-check executable")
    parser.add_argument("--shader-dir", type=Path, help="use an existing installed shader tree")
    parser.add_argument("--manifest-url", default=os.environ.get("VKHOOK_EFFECT_PACKAGES_URL", DEFAULT_MANIFEST_URL))
    args = parser.parse_args()

    if not args.shader_check.is_file():
        parser.error(f"shader checker does not exist: {args.shader_check}")
    if args.shader_dir and not args.shader_dir.is_dir():
        parser.error(f"shader directory does not exist: {args.shader_dir}")

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="vkhook-shader-tests-") as temporary:
        work_dir = Path(temporary)
        manifest = work_dir / "EffectPackages.ini"
        try:
            fetch_manifest(args.manifest_url, manifest)
        except Exception as error:
            print(f"Could not fetch EffectPackages.ini: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1

        shader_dir = args.shader_dir
        if shader_dir is None:
            shader_dir = work_dir / "Shaders"
            try:
                install_manifest_packages(manifest, work_dir, shader_dir)
            except Exception as error:
                print(error, file=sys.stderr)
                return 1

        return compile_shaders(args.shader_check.resolve(), shader_dir.resolve())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

`src/tests/test_shared_texture_smoke.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Opt-in GPU regression; needs Python 3, libX11, DISPLAY and an Xlib vkcube.

Usage: python3 src/tests/test_shared_texture_smoke.py --layer /abs/libvkhook.so
Supply --vkcube /path/to/32-bit/vkcube with a matching 32-bit layer if desired.
No desktop screenshots, global key injection, or user configuration writes.
"""

import argparse
import ctypes as C
import ctypes.util
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time


class XImage(C.Structure):
    _fields_ = [(name, kind) for name, kind in (
        ("width", C.c_int), ("height", C.c_int), ("xoffset", C.c_int),
        ("format", C.c_int), ("data", C.c_void_p), ("byte_order", C.c_int),
        ("bitmap_unit", C.c_int), ("bitmap_bit_order", C.c_int),
        ("bitmap_pad", C.c_int), ("depth", C.c_int),
        ("bytes_per_line", C.c_int), ("bits_per_pixel", C.c_int),
        ("red_mask", C.c_ulong), ("green_mask", C.c_ulong),
        ("blue_mask", C.c_ulong))]


class ClientMessage(C.Structure):
    _fields_ = [("type", C.c_int), ("serial", C.c_ulong),
                ("send_event", C.c_int), ("display", C.c_void_p),
                ("window", C.c_ulong), ("message_type", C.c_ulong),
                ("format", C.c_int), ("data", C.c_long * 5)]


class XEvent(C.Union):
    _fields_ = [("client", ClientMessage), ("padding", C.c_long * 24)]


class X11:
    def __init__(self):
        self.lib = C.CDLL(ctypes.util.find_library("X11") or "libX11.so.6")
        ptr, ul, integer = C.c_void_p, C.c_ulong, C.c_int
        signatures = {
            "XOpenDisplay": (ptr, [C.c_char_p]),
            "XCloseDisplay": (integer, [ptr]),
            "XDefaultRootWindow": (ul, [ptr]),
            "XQueryTree": (integer, [ptr, ul, C.POINTER(ul), C.POINTER(ul),
                                      C.POINTER(C.POINTER(ul)), C.POINTER(C.c_uint)]),
            "XFetchName": (integer, [ptr, ul, C.POINTER(ptr)]),
            "XFree": (integer, [ptr]),
            "XInternAtom": (ul, [ptr, C.c_char_p, integer]),
            "XGetWindowProperty": (integer, [ptr, ul, ul, C.c_long, C.c_long,
                integer, ul, C.POINTER(ul), C.POINTER(integer), C.POINTER(ul),
                C.POINTER(ul), C.POINTER(ptr)]),
            "XGetGeometry": (integer, [ptr, ul, C.POINTER(ul),
                C.POINTER(integer), C.POINTER(integer), C.POINTER(C.c_uint),
                C.POINTER(C.c_uint), C.POINTER(C.c_uint), C.POINTER(C.c_uint)]),
            "XGetImage": (C.POINTER(XImage), [ptr, ul, integer, integer,
                                               C.c_uint, C.c_uint, ul, integer]),
            "XGetPixel": (ul, [C.POINTER(XImage), integer, integer]),
            "XDestroyImage": (integer, [C.POINTER(XImage)]),
            "XSendEvent": (integer, [ptr, ul, integer, C.c_long, C.POINTER(XEvent)]),
            "XFlush": (integer, [ptr]),
        }
        for name, (result, arguments) in signatures.items():
            function = getattr(self.lib, name)
            function.restype, function.argtypes = result, arguments
        # A window can disappear between discovery and capture. Do not let the
        # default Xlib error handler terminate Python and bypass child cleanup.
        callback = C.CFUNCTYPE(integer, ptr, ptr)
        self.error_handler = callback(lambda display, event: 0)
        self.lib.XSetErrorHandler.argtypes = [callback]
        self.lib.XSetErrorHandler.restype = ptr
        self.lib.XSetErrorHandler(self.error_handler)
        self.display = self.lib.XOpenDisplay(None)
        if not self.display:
            raise RuntimeError("cannot open DISPLAY; provide DISPLAY/XAUTHORITY (or xvfb-run)")
        self.root = self.lib.XDefaultRootWindow(self.display)

    def windows(self):
        pending, found = [self.root], set()
        while pending:
            window = pending.pop()
            if window in found:
                continue
            found.add(window)
            root, parent = C.c_ulong(), C.c_ulong()
            children, count = C.POINTER(C.c_ulong)(), C.c_uint()
            if self.lib.XQueryTree(self.display, window, C.byref(root), C.byref(parent),
                                   C.byref(children), C.byref(count)):
                pending.extend(children[i] for i in range(count.value))
            if children:
                self.lib.XFree(children)
        return found

    def name(self, window):
        value = C.c_void_p()
        self.lib.XFetchName(self.display, window, C.byref(value))
        try:
            return C.string_at(value).decode(errors="replace") if value.value else ""
        finally:
            if value.value:
                self.lib.XFree(value)

    def pid(self, window):
        atom = self.lib.XInternAtom(self.display, b"_NET_WM_PID", 1)
        if not atom:
            return None
        kind, count, remaining = C.c_ulong(), C.c_ulong(), C.c_ulong()
        fmt, value = C.c_int(), C.c_void_p()
        self.lib.XGetWindowProperty(self.display, window, atom, 0, 1, 0, 6,
            C.byref(kind), C.byref(fmt), C.byref(count), C.byref(remaining), C.byref(value))
        try:
            if value.value and fmt.value == 32 and count.value == 1:
                return C.cast(value, C.POINTER(C.c_ulong))[0]
            return None
        finally:
            if value.value:
                self.lib.XFree(value)

    def size(self, window):
        root, x, y = C.c_ulong(), C.c_int(), C.c_int()
        width, height, border, depth = (C.c_uint() for _ in range(4))
        if not self.lib.XGetGeometry(self.display, window, C.byref(root), C.byref(x),
                C.byref(y), C.byref(width), C.byref(height), C.byref(border), C.byref(depth)):
            return None
        return width.value, height.value

    def sample(self, window):
        size = self.size(window)
        if size is None or min(size) < 16:
            return None
        width, height = size
        # Capture only the identified client window; never the root/desktop.
        image = self.lib.XGetImage(self.display, window, 0, 0,
                                   width, height, C.c_ulong(-1), 2)
        if not image:
            return None
        try:
            masks = (image.contents.red_mask, image.contents.green_mask, image.contents.blue_mask)
            if not all(masks):
                raise RuntimeError("XGetImage did not provide RGB masks (TrueColor display required)")
            shifts = [(mask & -mask).bit_length() - 1 for mask in masks]
            pixels = []
            for fy in (1, 2, 3):
                for fx in (1, 2, 3):
                    px, py = width * fx // 4, height * fy // 4
                    pixel = self.lib.XGetPixel(image, px, py)
                    rgb = [round(((pixel & mask) >> shift) * 255 / (mask >> shift))
                           for mask, shift in zip(masks, shifts)]
                    pixels.append({"xy": [px, py], "rgb": rgb})
            return pixels
        finally:
            self.lib.XDestroyImage(image)

    def close_window(self, window):
        event = XEvent()
        event.client.type = 33  # ClientMessage, directed only to our own window.
        event.client.display = self.display
        event.client.window = window
        event.client.message_type = self.lib.XInternAtom(self.display, b"WM_PROTOCOLS", 0)
        event.client.format = 32
        event.client.data[0] = self.lib.XInternAtom(self.display, b"WM_DELETE_WINDOW", 0)
        event.client.data[1] = 0  # CurrentTime
        self.lib.XSendEvent(self.display, window, 0, 0, C.byref(event))
        self.lib.XFlush(self.display)

    def close(self):
        self.lib.XCloseDisplay(self.display)


def seed(work, layer, executable):
    layer_dir, config = work / "layers", work / "config" / "VkHook"
    profiles = config / "configs" / "shaders"
    shaders = config / "reshade" / "Shaders"
    for directory in (layer_dir, profiles, shaders, work / "home", work / "data", work / "cache"):
        directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    layer_name = "VK_LAYER_VKHOOK_post_processing"
    manifest = {"file_format_version": "1.0.0", "layer": {
        "name": layer_name, "type": "GLOBAL", "library_path": str(layer),
        "api_version": "1.3.223", "implementation_version": "1",
        "description": "VkHook shared texture GPU regression",
        "functions": {"vkGetInstanceProcAddr": "VkHook_GetInstanceProcAddr",
                      "vkGetDeviceProcAddr": "VkHook_GetDeviceProcAddr"}}}
    # Deliberately no disable_environment: DISABLE_VKHOOK disables installed
    # implicit manifests, not this explicitly requested test manifest.
    (layer_dir / "VkHook.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest), encoding="utf-8")
    names = ("SharedTextureProducer", "SharedTextureConsumer")
    for name in names:
        shutil.copyfile(Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "fixtures" / (name + ".fx"),
                        shaders / (name + ".fx"))
    (config / "VkHook.conf").write_text(
        "enableOnLaunch = true\noverlayKey = Home\nreloadKey = F10\n"
        "maxEffects = 10\nautoApply = false\ndepthCapture = on\nshowDebugWindow = false\n",
        encoding="utf-8")
    # The layer keys profiles by the resolved /proc/self/exe basename, including
    # custom 32-bit binary names, not argv[0] or a hard-coded 'vkcube'.
    game = executable.name
    (config / "configs" / (game + ".conf")).write_text(
        "".join(name + " = " + name + ".fx\n" for name in names) +
        "effects = " + ":".join(names) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    techniques = ",".join(name + "@" + name + ".fx" for name in names)
    (profiles / (game + "@shared-texture.ini")).write_text(
        "Techniques=" + techniques + "\nTechniqueSorting=" + techniques + "\n" +
        "".join("\n[" + name + ".fx]\n" for name in names), encoding="utf-8")
    (profiles / (game + ".last-profile")).write_text("shared-texture\n", encoding="utf-8")
    env = {key: value for key, value in os.environ.items()
           if not key.startswith(("VKHOOK_", "VK_LAYER_", "VK_ADD_LAYER_", "VK_LOADER_LAYERS_"))
           and key not in ("VK_INSTANCE_LAYERS", "ENABLE_VKHOOK", "DISABLE_VKHOOK")}
    # Preserve default X authentication before replacing HOME for the child.
    authority = Path(os.environ.get("HOME", "")) / ".Xauthority"
    if "XAUTHORITY" not in env and authority.is_file():
        env["XAUTHORITY"] = str(authority.resolve())
    env.update(HOME=str(work / "home"), XDG_CONFIG_HOME=str(work / "config"),
               XDG_DATA_HOME=str(work / "data"), XDG_CACHE_HOME=str(work / "cache"),
               VK_LAYER_PATH=str(layer_dir), VK_INSTANCE_LAYERS=layer_name,
               VK_LOADER_LAYERS_DISABLE="~implicit", DISABLE_VKHOOK="1",
               VK_LOADER_DEBUG="layer", VKHOOK_LOG_LEVEL="debug")
    return env


def stop(child, x11, window):
    if child.poll() is not None:
        return
    if window is not None:
        x11.close_window(window)
        try:
            child.wait(timeout=5)
            return
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            pass
    child.terminate()
    try:
        child.wait(timeout=3)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        child.kill()
        child.wait()


def diagnostics(work, artifacts, samples):
    print("Last sampled pixels: " + json.dumps(samples), flush=True)
    for path in sorted(work.rglob("*.log")):
        print("--- " + str(path.relative_to(work)) + " (last 64 KiB) ---", flush=True)
        print(path.read_text(errors="replace")[-65536:], flush=True)
    if artifacts:
        artifacts.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        destination = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="shared-texture-", dir=artifacts))
        for path in work.rglob("*.log"):
            target = destination / path.relative_to(work)
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            shutil.copyfile(path, target)
        (destination / "pixels.json").write_text(json.dumps(samples, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        print("Failure artifacts: " + str(destination), flush=True)


def run(args, executable):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="vkhook-shared-texture-") as temporary:
        work = Path(temporary)
        child, x11, window, samples = None, None, None, None
        try:
            env = seed(work, args.layer, executable)
            x11 = X11()
            previous = x11.windows()
            with (work / "vkcube.log").open("wb") as output:
                child = subprocess.Popen([str(executable), "--wsi", "xlib", "--width", "640", "--height", "480"], env=env,
                                         stdout=output, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
                deadline, consecutive = time.monotonic() + args.timeout, 0
                while time.monotonic() < deadline:
                    if child.poll() is not None:
                        raise RuntimeError("vkcube exited before contents passed: " + str(child.returncode))
                    if window is None:
                        candidates = []
                        for candidate in x11.windows() - previous:
                            title = x11.name(candidate).lower()
                            owner = x11.pid(candidate)
                            if owner is not None and owner != child.pid:
                                continue
                            if ("vulkan cube" in title or "vkcube" in title or owner == child.pid
                                    or x11.size(candidate) == (640, 480)):
                                candidates.append(candidate)
                        if len(candidates) > 1:
                            raise RuntimeError("multiple new cube windows; refusing an ambiguous capture")
                        if candidates:
                            window = candidates[0]
                            print("Capturing new vkcube window: " + hex(window), flush=True)
                    if window is not None:
                        samples = x11.sample(window)
                        green = samples and all(r <= 12 and g >= 243 and b <= 12
                                                for r, g, b in (p["rgb"] for p in samples))
                        consecutive = consecutive + 1 if green else 0
                        if consecutive == 3:
                            break
                    time.sleep(0.2)
                else:
                    raise RuntimeError("timed out waiting for producer green (0,255,0) in consumer; "
                                       "keep the test window visible and unobscured")
                # Pixel contents are the assertion, but also establish that the
                # requested build, not an installed layer, actually participated.
                if str(args.layer) not in (work / "vkcube.log").read_text(errors="replace"):
                    raise RuntimeError("loader trace does not identify the requested layer library")
                if not (work / "config" / "VkHook" / "vkhook.log").is_file():
                    raise RuntimeError("requested layer produced no initialization log")
                stop(child, x11, window)
                if child.returncode != 0:
                    raise RuntimeError("vkcube did not shut down cleanly: " + str(child.returncode))
            print("PASS: producer-to-consumer shared texture contents; sampled pixels: " +
                  json.dumps(samples), flush=True)
            return 0
        except (OSError, RuntimeError, KeyboardInterrupt) as error:
            if child is not None:
                stop(child, x11, window)
            print("FAIL: " + (str(error) or type(error).__name__), flush=True)
            diagnostics(work, args.artifacts, samples)
            return 130 if isinstance(error, KeyboardInterrupt) else 1
        finally:
            if child is not None and child.poll() is None:
                stop(child, x11, window)
            if x11 is not None:
                x11.close()


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("--layer", type=Path, required=True, help="absolute path to libvkhook.so under test")
    parser.add_argument("--vkcube", default="vkcube", help="Xlib-capable vkcube executable (default: vkcube)")
    parser.add_argument("--timeout", type=float, default=30, help="window/contents readiness deadline in seconds (default: 30)")
    parser.add_argument("--artifacts", type=Path, help="optional directory for failure logs/pixels; otherwise stdout only")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if not args.layer.is_absolute() or not args.layer.is_file():
        parser.error("--layer must name an existing absolute library path")
    args.layer = args.layer.resolve()
    if not 0 < args.timeout <= 300:
        parser.error("--timeout must be greater than zero and at most 300 seconds")
    executable = shutil.which(args.vkcube)
    if not executable:
        parser.error("vkcube executable not found: " + args.vkcube)
    if not os.environ.get("DISPLAY"):
        parser.error("DISPLAY is required; run on X11/Xwayland or under xvfb-run")
    return run(args, Path(executable).resolve())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

`src/tests/variable_font_test.cc`:

```cc
// Headless tests for the stb_truetype variable-font extension: fvar parsing,
// axis normalization, gvar outlines and HVAR advances. The two shipped faces are
// committed, so this guards them against a bad download or a regression in the
// variation code without needing a GPU.

#define STB_TRUETYPE_IMPLEMENTATION
#include "imstb_truetype.h"

#include <cmath>
#include <cstdio>
#include <fstream>
#include <iterator>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

static int g_checks = 0;
static int g_failures = 0;

static void expect(bool condition, const char* what)
{
    g_checks++;
    if (!condition)
    {
        g_failures++;
        std::printf("FAIL: %s\n", what);
    }
}

#define TAG(a, b, c, d) ((stbtt_uint32)(((unsigned)(a) << 24) | ((unsigned)(b) << 16) | ((unsigned)(c) << 8) | (unsigned)(d)))

static std::vector<unsigned char> loadFile(const char* path)
{
    std::ifstream f(path, std::ios::binary);
    if (!f.good())
        return {};
    return std::vector<unsigned char>((std::istreambuf_iterator<char>(f)), std::istreambuf_iterator<char>());
}

static const char* findFont(const char* name)
{
    static std::string resolved;
    const char* prefixes[] = {"assets/font/", "../assets/font/", "../../assets/font/"};
    for (const char* p : prefixes)
    {
        resolved = std::string(p) + name;
        std::ifstream probe(resolved);
        if (probe.good())
            return resolved.c_str();
    }
    return nullptr;
}

static int axisIndex(const stbtt_fontinfo* info, stbtt_uint32 tag)
{
    const int n = stbtt_GetVariationAxisCount(info);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
        if (stbtt_GetVariationAxisTag(info, i) == tag)
            return i;
    return -1;
}

static void setAxis(stbtt_fontinfo* info, stbtt_uint32 tag, float value)
{
    stbtt_SetVariationCoords(info, &tag, &value, 1);
}

static long shapeHash(const stbtt_fontinfo* info, int glyph)
{
    stbtt_vertex* v = 0;
    const int n = stbtt_GetGlyphShape(info, glyph, &v);
    long h = 1469598103L;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
        h = h * 131 + v[i].x * 7 + v[i].y * 13 + v[i].cx * 3 + v[i].cy * 5 + v[i].type;
    stbtt_FreeShape(info, v);
    return h;
}

static int glyphAdvance(const stbtt_fontinfo* info, int glyph)
{
    int a = 0;
    stbtt_GetGlyphHMetrics(info, glyph, &a, 0);
    return a;
}

static void testFace(const char* name, int expected_axes, float wght_min, float wght_def, float wght_max,
                     bool has_rond, bool has_wdth)
{
    const char* path = findFont(name);
    if (!path)
    {
        std::printf("SKIP: %s not found next to the build\n", name);
        return;
    }
    std::vector<unsigned char> buf = loadFile(path);
    expect(!buf.empty(), "variable font file reads");

    stbtt_fontinfo info;
    expect(stbtt_InitFont(&info, buf.data(), stbtt_GetFontOffsetForIndex(buf.data(), 0)) != 0,
           "variable font parses");
    expect(info.hasVariations == 1, "font reports variations");

    const int axis_count = stbtt_GetVariationAxisCount(&info);
    char msg[128];
    std::snprintf(msg, sizeof(msg), "%s exposes %d axes", name, expected_axes);
    expect(axis_count == expected_axes, msg);

    const int wi = axisIndex(&info, TAG('w', 'g', 'h', 't'));
    expect(wi >= 0, "wght axis is present");
    expect(std::fabs(stbtt_GetVariationAxisMin(&info, wi) - wght_min) < 0.5f, "wght min matches");
    expect(std::fabs(stbtt_GetVariationAxisDefault(&info, wi) - wght_def) < 0.5f, "wght default matches");
    expect(std::fabs(stbtt_GetVariationAxisMax(&info, wi) - wght_max) < 0.5f, "wght max matches");
    expect(axisIndex(&info, TAG('R', 'O', 'N', 'D')) >= 0 == has_rond, "ROND axis presence matches");
    expect(axisIndex(&info, TAG('w', 'd', 't', 'h')) >= 0 == has_wdth, "wdth axis presence matches");

    const int gH = stbtt_FindGlyphIndex(&info, 'H');
    expect(gH > 0, "glyph 'H' resolves");

    // baseline (no coords) is the default instance.
    const long base_shape = shapeHash(&info, gH);
    int x0, y0, x1, y1;
    stbtt_GetGlyphBox(&info, gH, &x0, &y0, &x1, &y1);
    const int base_h = y1 - y0;

    // heavier weight changes the outline (gvar deltas are applied).
    setAxis(&info, TAG('w', 'g', 'h', 't'), wght_max);
    const long heavy_shape = shapeHash(&info, gH);
    expect(heavy_shape != base_shape, "gvar changes the outline at a different weight");
    stbtt_GetGlyphBox(&info, gH, &x0, &y0, &x1, &y1);
    expect((y1 - y0) >= base_h, "a heavier weight does not shrink the glyph box");

    // setting the default coordinate reproduces the default instance.
    setAxis(&info, TAG('w', 'g', 'h', 't'), wght_def);
    expect(shapeHash(&info, gH) == base_shape, "resetting to the default reproduces the base outline");

    if (has_wdth)
    {
        const int wi2 = axisIndex(&info, TAG('w', 'd', 't', 'h'));
        setAxis(&info, TAG('w', 'd', 't', 'h'), stbtt_GetVariationAxisMin(&info, wi2));
        const int narrow = glyphAdvance(&info, gH);
        setAxis(&info, TAG('w', 'd', 't', 'h'), stbtt_GetVariationAxisMax(&info, wi2));
        const int wide = glyphAdvance(&info, gH);
        expect(wide > narrow, "HVAR widens the advance along the width axis");
    }

    if (has_rond)
    {
        setAxis(&info, TAG('R', 'O', 'N', 'D'), 0.0f);
        const long square = shapeHash(&info, gH);
        setAxis(&info, TAG('R', 'O', 'N', 'D'), 100.0f);
        const long rounded = shapeHash(&info, gH);
        expect(square != rounded, "ROND changes the outline (rounded document cut)");
    }
}

int main()
{
    testFace("GoogleSansFlex.ttf", 6, 1.0f, 400.0f, 1000.0f, /*rond*/ true, /*wdth*/ true);
    testFace("RobotoFlex.ttf", 13, 100.0f, 400.0f, 1000.0f, /*rond*/ false, /*wdth*/ true);

    // A static face must degrade cleanly: zero axes, coords are a no-op.
    const char* icon = findFont("MaterialSymbolsRounded.ttf");
    if (icon)
    {
        std::vector<unsigned char> buf = loadFile(icon);
        stbtt_fontinfo info;
        stbtt_InitFont(&info, buf.data(), 0);
        expect(stbtt_GetVariationAxisCount(&info) == 0, "a static instance reports no axes");
        setAxis(&info, TAG('w', 'g', 'h', 't'), 900.0f); // must not crash / must be ignored
        expect(shapeHash(&info, stbtt_FindGlyphIndex(&info, 0xE5CA)) != 0, "static outline still builds");
    }

    std::printf("%d checks, %d failures\n", g_checks, g_failures);
    return g_failures == 0 ? 0 : 1;
}
```

`src/tests/wayland_interpose_patch_test.cc`:

```cc
// glibc rewrites the dynamic section's pointer entries (DT_SYMTAB, DT_STRTAB,
// DT_JMPREL) to absolute addresses in place at load time. A patcher that adds
// the load base again dereferences a non-canonical pointer and takes the whole
// client down. This drives the real scan against a real libwayland and
// requires the GOT slot's current value to match dlsym. Build this test for
// both native ELF classes: i386 uses REL, while x86_64 uses RELA. Libraries
// built with -fno-plt use GLOB_DAT rather than a PLT JUMP_SLOT relocation.
#include "wayland_interpose_patch.hh"

#include <dlfcn.h>

#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>

namespace
{
    int failures = 0;

    void check(bool ok, const char* what)
    {
        std::printf("%s %s\n", ok ? "ok  " : "FAIL", what);
        if (!ok)
            ++failures;
    }
}

int main()
{
    const char* override = std::getenv("VKHOOK_TEST_WAYLAND_LIB");
    void* handle = override ? dlopen(override, RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL)
                            : dlopen("libwayland-client.so.0", RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL);
    if (!handle)
    {
        std::printf("SKIP no libwayland available to scan\n");
        return 77;
    }

    void* slot = nullptr;
    void* real = nullptr;
    check(VkHook::waylandMarshalSlotForTests(&slot, &real), "marshal GOT slot located without faulting");
    if (!slot)
    {
        std::printf("%d failure(s)\n", failures ? failures : 1);
        return 1;
    }

    void* direct = dlsym(handle, "wl_proxy_marshal_array_flags");
    check(direct != nullptr, "dlsym resolves the marshal entry");
    check(real == direct, "slot's value is the real marshal entry");
    check(*static_cast<void**>(slot) == direct, "slot memory holds the real marshal entry");

    std::printf("%d failure(s)\n", failures);
    return failures == 0 ? 0 : 1;
}
```

`src/tests/wayland_syncobj_gate_test.cc`:

```cc
// A missing hold here ends as a compositor-killed wayland connection at
// runtime, so the present/commit ordering is driven directly with threads.
#include "wayland_syncobj_gate.hh"

#include <atomic>
#include <chrono>
#include <cstdio>
#include <thread>

using namespace VkHook::WaylandSyncobjGate;
using Clock = std::chrono::steady_clock;

namespace
{
    int failures = 0;

    void check(bool ok, const char* what, int line)
    {
        if (!ok)
        {
            ++failures;
            std::fprintf(stderr, "FAIL:%d: %s\n", line, what);
        }
    }

    uint64_t microsSince(Clock::time_point start)
    {
        return std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::microseconds>(Clock::now() - start).count();
    }
} // namespace

#define CHECK(cond) check((cond), #cond, __LINE__)

int main()
{
    constexpr uint32_t SURFACE = 43;

    // no present open: commits pass straight through
    {
        resetForTests();
        auto start = Clock::now();
        beginCommit(SURFACE);
        CHECK(microsSince(start) < 5000);
        CHECK(heldCount() == 0);
    }

    // the presenter's own commit inside its present is never held
    {
        resetForTests();
        beginPresent(SURFACE);
        auto start = Clock::now();
        beginCommit(SURFACE);
        CHECK(microsSince(start) < 5000);
        CHECK(heldCount() == 0);
        endPresent(SURFACE);
    }

    // a foreign commit waits until the presenter closes the bracket
    {
        resetForTests();
        std::atomic<bool> presentOpen{false};
        std::atomic<bool> presentFinished{false};
        std::atomic<uint64_t> foreignWait{0};

        std::thread presenter([&] {
            beginPresent(SURFACE);
            presentOpen.store(true);
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(40));
            presentFinished.store(true);
            endPresent(SURFACE);
        });

        while (!presentOpen.load())
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));

        std::thread foreign([&] {
            auto start = Clock::now();
            beginCommit(SURFACE);
            foreignWait.store(microsSince(start));
            CHECK(presentFinished.load()); // released only after the bracket closed
        });

        presenter.join();
        foreign.join();

        CHECK(foreignWait.load() >= 25000);
        CHECK(heldCount() == 1);

        // and once closed, commits pass instantly
        auto start = Clock::now();
        beginCommit(SURFACE);
        CHECK(microsSince(start) < 5000);
    }

    // endPresent from another thread must not close the bracket
    {
        resetForTests();
        setWaitBudgetForTests(20000);
        std::atomic<uint64_t> waited{0};
        std::atomic<bool> presentOpen{false};
        std::atomic<bool> finish{false};

        std::thread presenter([&] {
            beginPresent(SURFACE);
            presentOpen.store(true);
            while (!finish.load())
                std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
            endPresent(SURFACE);
        });

        while (!presentOpen.load())
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));

        endPresent(SURFACE); // different thread: ignored

        std::thread foreign([&] {
            auto start = Clock::now();
            beginCommit(SURFACE);
            waited.store(microsSince(start));
        });
        foreign.join();
        CHECK(waited.load() >= 18000);

        finish.store(true);
        presenter.join();
        resetForTests();
    }

    // bound: a present that never closes cannot park commits forever
    {
        resetForTests();
        setWaitBudgetForTests(20000);
        beginPresent(SURFACE); // opened by this thread, never ended

        std::atomic<uint64_t> first{0};
        std::atomic<uint64_t> second{0};

        std::thread a([&] {
            auto start = Clock::now();
            beginCommit(SURFACE);
            first.store(microsSince(start));
        });
        a.join();

        std::thread b([&] {
            auto start = Clock::now();
            beginCommit(SURFACE);
            second.store(microsSince(start));
        });
        b.join();

        CHECK(first.load() >= 18000);
        CHECK(first.load() < 500000);
        CHECK(second.load() >= 18000);
        CHECK(second.load() < 500000);
        CHECK(heldCount() == 2);

        resetForTests();
    }

    if (failures)
    {
        std::fprintf(stderr, "%d check(s) failed\n", failures);
        return 1;
    }
    std::printf("ok\n");
    return 0;
}
```

`src/tests/x11_input_handoff_test.cc`:

```cc
// X11 input blocking against the layer's real blocker: notifications capture only
// their hitbox, while an interactive menu owns pointer and keyboard until close.
// A held key must be released into the game on entry and restored on exit.
//
// It synthesises real input on the developer's display, so it only runs with
// VKHOOK_X11_INPUT_TEST=1 set; otherwise it reports SKIP (exit 77).
//
// usage: vkhook-x11-input-handoff-tests <path to libvkhook.so>

#include <X11/Xlib.h>
#include <X11/keysym.h>
#include <X11/extensions/XTest.h>
#include <dlfcn.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include "input/mouse_input.hh"

typedef void (*InitFn)(bool);
typedef void (*SetWindowFn)(unsigned long);
typedef void (*SetRectsFn)(const void*, int);
typedef void (*SetBoolFn)(bool);
typedef void (*SetPosFn)(float, float);
typedef VkHook::MouseState (*GetMouseFn)();

struct InputRect { float x, y, width, height; };

static void pump(Display* d, const char* tag, int* sawPress, int* sawRelease, int* sawGrabFocus)
{
    while (XPending(d) > 0)
    {
        XEvent ev;
        XNextEvent(d, &ev);
        if (ev.type == KeyPress)   { (*sawPress)++;   printf("    [%s] game: KeyPress keycode=%u\n", tag, ev.xkey.keycode); }
        if (ev.type == KeyRelease) { (*sawRelease)++; printf("    [%s] game: KeyRelease keycode=%u\n", tag, ev.xkey.keycode); }
        if ((ev.type == FocusIn || ev.type == FocusOut) && ev.xfocus.mode != 0)
        {
            (*sawGrabFocus)++;
            printf("    [%s] game: %s mode=%d (grab notification Wine reacts to)\n", tag,
                   ev.type == FocusIn ? "FocusIn" : "FocusOut", ev.xfocus.mode);
        }
    }
    fflush(stdout);
}

static const char* grabStatus(Display* probe, Window w, int keyboard)
{
    int status = keyboard
        ? XGrabKeyboard(probe, w, False, GrabModeAsync, GrabModeAsync, CurrentTime)
        : XGrabPointer(probe, w, False, ButtonPressMask, GrabModeAsync, GrabModeAsync, None, None, CurrentTime);
    if (keyboard) XUngrabKeyboard(probe, CurrentTime);
    else          XUngrabPointer(probe, CurrentTime);
    XSync(probe, False);
    return status == AlreadyGrabbed ? "held by the layer" : (status == GrabSuccess ? "free" : "other");
}

int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
    if (getenv("VKHOOK_X11_INPUT_TEST") == nullptr)
    {
        printf("skipped: set VKHOOK_X11_INPUT_TEST=1 to run (it synthesises real input)\n");
        return 77;
    }
    if (XOpenDisplay(NULL) == nullptr)
    {
        printf("skipped: no X display\n");
        return 77;
    }

    const char* libPath = argc > 1 ? argv[1] : "build/src/libvkhook.so";
    void* lib = dlopen(libPath, RTLD_NOW);
    if (!lib) { printf("dlopen failed: %s\n", dlerror()); return 1; }

    InitFn        initInputBlocker        = (InitFn) dlsym(lib, "_ZN6VkHook16initInputBlockerEb");
    SetWindowFn   setX11Window            = (SetWindowFn) dlsym(lib, "_ZN6VkHook12setX11WindowEm");
    SetRectsFn    setInputRects           = (SetRectsFn) dlsym(lib, "_ZN6VkHook13setInputRectsEPKNS_9InputRectEi");
    SetBoolFn     setInputBlocked         = (SetBoolFn) dlsym(lib, "_ZN6VkHook15setInputBlockedEb");
    SetBoolFn     setInputInteractive     = (SetBoolFn) dlsym(lib, "_ZN6VkHook19setInputInteractiveEb");
    SetBoolFn     setOverlayWantsKeyboard = (SetBoolFn) dlsym(lib, "_ZN6VkHook23setOverlayWantsKeyboardEb");
    SetPosFn      updatePointerPosition   = (SetPosFn) dlsym(lib, "_ZN6VkHook21updatePointerPositionEff");
    GetMouseFn getMouseState = (GetMouseFn) dlsym(lib, "_ZN6VkHook16getMouseStateX11Ev");
    if (!initInputBlocker || !setX11Window || !setInputRects || !setInputBlocked
        || !setInputInteractive || !setOverlayWantsKeyboard || !updatePointerPosition || !getMouseState)
    {
        printf("missing symbols: %s\n", dlerror());
        return 1;
    }

    Display* game = XOpenDisplay(NULL);
    Display* probe = XOpenDisplay(NULL);
    if (!game || !probe) { printf("no display\n"); return 1; }

    const Window root = DefaultRootWindow(game);
    const Window win = XCreateSimpleWindow(game, root, 90, 90, 380, 260, 0, 0, 0x101820);
    XSelectInput(game, win, KeyPressMask | KeyReleaseMask | FocusChangeMask | StructureNotifyMask);
    XStoreName(game, win, "vkhook input test");
    XMapWindow(game, win);
    XSync(game, False);
    usleep(300000);
    int p = 0, r = 0, f = 0;
    pump(game, "setup", &p, &r, &f);
    XSetInputFocus(game, win, RevertToParent, CurrentTime);
    XSync(game, False);
    usleep(150000);
    pump(game, "setup", &p, &r, &f);

    const KeyCode w = XKeysymToKeycode(game, XK_w);

    setX11Window((unsigned long)win);
    initInputBlocker(true);
    struct InputRect rect = {0.0f, 0.0f, 380.0f, 260.0f};
    setInputRects(&rect, 1);
    setInputBlocked(true);
    updatePointerPosition(100.0f, 100.0f);   // pointer over the overlay hitbox

    printf("\n1. pointer over the overlay: pointer grab taken, keyboard left alone\n");
    printf("    pointer grab : %s\n", grabStatus(probe, root, 0));
    printf("    keyboard grab: %s\n", grabStatus(probe, root, 1));
    int ok1 = strcmp(grabStatus(probe, root, 0), "held by the layer") == 0
           && strcmp(grabStatus(probe, root, 1), "free") == 0;

    printf("\n2. a key held across the keyboard grab is released into the game\n");
    XTestFakeKeyEvent(probe, w, True, 0);            // player presses w
    XSync(probe, False);
    usleep(150000);
    p = r = f = 0;
    pump(game, "held", &p, &r, &f);
    if (p == 0) { printf("    game never saw the press; aborting\n"); return 1; }

    updatePointerPosition(500.0f, 500.0f);           // outside every overlay hitbox
    setInputInteractive(true);                    // menu, without text-field focus
    usleep(200000);
    p = r = f = 0;
    pump(game, "grab-engaged", &p, &r, &f);
    printf("    keyboard grab: %s\n", grabStatus(probe, root, 1));
    int ok2 = r > 0 && strcmp(grabStatus(probe, root, 1), "held by the layer") == 0
           && strcmp(grabStatus(probe, root, 0), "held by the layer") == 0;

    printf("\n3. leaving a text field does not release the open menu's capture\n");
    setOverlayWantsKeyboard(true);
    setOverlayWantsKeyboard(false);
    int ok3 = strcmp(grabStatus(probe, root, 1), "held by the layer") == 0
           && strcmp(grabStatus(probe, root, 0), "held by the layer") == 0;

    printf("\n4. captured raw motion is independent of game cursor warps\n");
    XTestFakeRelativeMotionEvent(probe, -10000, -10000, 0);
    XSync(probe, False);
    usleep(50000);
    const auto origin = getMouseState();
    XTestFakeRelativeMotionEvent(probe, 35, 20, 0);
    XSync(probe, False);
    usleep(50000);
    const auto moved = getMouseState();
    XWarpPointer(game, None, win, 0, 0, 0, 0, 190, 130);
    XSync(game, False);
    usleep(50000);
    const auto warped = getMouseState();
    int okMotion = moved.x == origin.x + 35 && moved.y == origin.y + 20
                && warped.x == moved.x && warped.y == moved.y;
    printf("    origin=%d,%d moved=%d,%d after warp=%d,%d\n",
           origin.x, origin.y, moved.x, moved.y, warped.x, warped.y);

    printf("\n5. captured buttons release and wheel ticks are consumed once\n");
    XTestFakeButtonEvent(probe, 1, True, 0);
    XSync(probe, False);
    usleep(50000);
    const auto heldMouse = getMouseState();
    XTestFakeButtonEvent(probe, 1, False, 0);
    XTestFakeButtonEvent(probe, 5, True, 0);
    XTestFakeButtonEvent(probe, 5, False, 0);
    XSync(probe, False);
    usleep(50000);
    const auto releasedMouse = getMouseState();
    const auto drainedMouse = getMouseState();
    int okMouse = heldMouse.leftButton && !releasedMouse.leftButton
               && releasedMouse.scrollDelta == -1.0f && drainedMouse.scrollDelta == 0.0f;

    printf("\n6. closing the menu hands still-held keys back\n");
    setInputInteractive(false);
    setInputBlocked(false);
    usleep(200000);
    p = r = f = 0;
    pump(game, "grab-released", &p, &r, &f);
    printf("    keyboard grab: %s\n", grabStatus(probe, root, 1));
    int ok4 = p > 0 && strcmp(grabStatus(probe, root, 1), "free") == 0
           && strcmp(grabStatus(probe, root, 0), "free") == 0;

    // clean up the simulated physical key
    XTestFakeKeyEvent(probe, w, False, 0);
    XSync(probe, False);
    pump(game, "cleanup", &p, &r, &f);

    printf("\nresult: notification=%s entry=%s ownership=%s motion=%s mouse=%s exit=%s\n",
           ok1 ? "PASS" : "FAIL", ok2 ? "PASS" : "FAIL", ok3 ? "PASS" : "FAIL",
           okMotion ? "PASS" : "FAIL", okMouse ? "PASS" : "FAIL", ok4 ? "PASS" : "FAIL");
    printf("%s\n", (ok1 && ok2 && ok3 && okMotion && okMouse && ok4) ? "ALL PASS" : "FAILURES PRESENT");

    XDestroyWindow(game, win);
    XCloseDisplay(probe);
    XCloseDisplay(game);
    return (ok1 && ok2 && ok3 && okMotion && okMouse && ok4) ? 0 : 1;
}
```

`src/vendor/imgui/README.md`:

```md
### Dear ImGui used by VkHook

The vendored core is Dear ImGui **1.92.6 WIP** (`IMGUI_VERSION_NUM` 19258),
from the upstream docking branch at
[`396b33d0d011290f11915b6a2a2bf7737fb42dd7`](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui/tree/396b33d0d011290f11915b6a2a2bf7737fb42dd7).
Widgets, scrollbars, navigation focus indicators and window titles use upstream
rendering and interaction rather than custom theme hooks.

VkHook retains its variable-font axis extensions in `imgui.h`,
`imgui_draw.cc` and `imstb_truetype.h`, right-button window resizing, and its
Vulkan backend changes. The runtime uses ImGui's embedded default font; setup
does not download or install interface fonts. Optional font fixtures and their
licenses remain separate from the runtime for the variable-font tests.

### repository integration

This directory is tracked as a squashed Git subtree of
[`buwryme/imgui-material-3`](https://github.com/buwryme/imgui-material-3), initially
imported at `80b80599b864489b78b6692a39ed7709c3404b2a`. That fork supplies the
file layout and extensions; local commits remove its Material theme and
restore the upstream widgets described above. This is not a direct subtree of
`ocornut/imgui`. See the repository's `docs/WORKFLOWS.md` for updates and patch
export. No submodule initialization is required.

### license
ImGui is licensed under the MIT License, see [LICENSE.txt](LICENSE.txt). the modifications that this repository has are under that license too.
```

`src/vendor/imgui/backends/imgui_impl_vulkan.cc`:

```cc
// dear imgui: Renderer Backend for Vulkan
// This needs to be used along with a Platform Backend (e.g. GLFW, SDL, Win32, custom..)

// Implemented features:
//  [!] Renderer: User texture binding. Use 'VkDescriptorSet' as texture identifier. Call ImGui_ImplVulkan_AddTexture() to register one. Read the FAQ about ImTextureID/ImTextureRef + https://github.com/ocornut/imgui/pull/914 for discussions.
//  [X] Renderer: Large meshes support (64k+ vertices) even with 16-bit indices (ImGuiBackendFlags_RendererHasVtxOffset).
//  [X] Renderer: Texture updates support for dynamic font atlas (ImGuiBackendFlags_RendererHasTextures).
//  [X] Renderer: Expose selected render state for draw callbacks to use. Access in '(ImGui_ImplXXXX_RenderState*)GetPlatformIO().Renderer_RenderState'.
//  [x] Renderer: Multi-viewport / platform windows. With issues (flickering when creating a new viewport).

// The aim of imgui_impl_vulkan.h/.cpp is to be usable in your engine without any modification.
// IF YOU FEEL YOU NEED TO MAKE ANY CHANGE TO THIS CODE, please share them and your feedback at https://github.com/ocornut/imgui/

// You can use unmodified imgui_impl_* files in your project. See examples/ folder for examples of using this.
// Prefer including the entire imgui/ repository into your project (either as a copy or as a submodule), and only build the backends you need.
// Learn about Dear ImGui:
// - FAQ                  https://dearimgui.com/faq
// - Getting Started      https://dearimgui.com/getting-started
// - Documentation        https://dearimgui.com/docs (same as your local docs/ folder).
// - Introduction, links and more at the top of imgui.cpp

// Important note to the reader who wish to integrate imgui_impl_vulkan.cpp/.h in their own engine/app.
// - Common ImGui_ImplVulkan_XXX functions and structures are used to interface with imgui_impl_vulkan.cpp/.h.
//   You will use those if you want to use this rendering backend in your engine/app.
// - Helper ImGui_ImplVulkanH_XXX functions and structures are only used by this example (main.cpp) and by
//   the backend itself (imgui_impl_vulkan.cpp), but should PROBABLY NOT be used by your own engine/app code.
// Read comments in imgui_impl_vulkan.h.

// CHANGELOG
// (minor and older changes stripped away, please see git history for details)
```
